- Deps: `entireio/auth-go`, `entireio/external-agents`, `entireio/cli-checkpoints`.
- `api` command routes `--to core` (entire-core) vs `--to cell` (Go entire-api).
- **Checkpoint model**: ephemeral checkpoints on per-worktree shadow branch
  `entire/<HEAD:7>-<worktree:6>` (intra-session rewind); persistent ones condensed onto
  `entire/checkpoints/v1`. Pluggable backends: git-branch (legacy) vs git-refs
  (one-ref-per-checkpoint) via `ENTIRE_CHECKPOINTS_PRIMARY`/`_MIRRORS`. Session state in
  `.git/entire-sessions/` (shared across worktrees). Transcripts: `full.jsonl` (raw,
  authoritative) + compacted `transcript.jsonl`. OPF (OpenAI Privacy Filter) = pre-push
  redaction layer rewriting unpushed v1 commits (`Entire-OPF-Applied: true`).
- **Test isolation rules** (enforced): never real CWD `.git` / `~/.config/entire` /
  keychain — `testutil.InitRepo` + `ENTIRE_CONFIG_DIR` overrides; `t.Parallel()` unless

## 8. Auth & identity flow

1. `entire-core` (in entiredb) is the identity provider: OAuth/OIDC, mints JWTs, exposes JWKS.
2. CLI + web log in against Core, receive JWTs; jurisdiction-scoped access via RFC 8693 STS
   token exchange (`cross_juris_transport`, `cell_target`).
3. Cells (`entire-api`) verify bearer JWTs against Core JWKS; authz via regional SpiceDB.
4. Service-to-service = mTLS (cells → entiredb Repo API; `core/repofacts` Connect; git-meta-service).

## 10. Key ADRs / gotchas

- entiredb: **no Raft** (`20260320-no-raft`), reserved refs `refs/meta/entire/*`
  (`20260603-reserved-refs`), entire-api split (`20260622`).
- Two distinct "api": Go **`entire-api`** (cells) vs TS **`entire.io/api`** (BFF). Don't conflate.
- Content is never copied into product stores — always read-through to entiredb by branch tip.
- `start-dev.sh` carries stale Rails + Raft labels (see §3).
- Root `README.md`/`Onboarding.md` say setup clones "entire" — `setup-repos.sh` actually
  clones `entiredb` + `entire.io` + `cli`. Docs drifted.

## 11. git-meta-service (detail)

- Implements the [git-meta](https://git-meta.com) exchange format as an API: `(target,key,value)`
  metadata (string/list/set) on commits/branches/paths/change-ids/project, byte-compatible with
  the upstream Rust `git meta` CLI (golden test round-trips vs real CLI if installed).
- **Write path**: serialize → CAS-push to `refs/meta/main` in entiredb (go-git v6 smart HTTP,
  forwards caller's JWT so push authz matches) → materialize into Postgres read-model. Git is
  source of truth; Postgres rebuildable. NATS consumer materializes out-of-band CLI pushes
  (read-only mTLS identity).
- **API** `/api/v1/repos/{repoId}/meta/*`: set/rm, list push/rm, set add/rm, cas (412 precondition /
  409 ref-race), GET query (`target`/`key`/`prefix`). Huma v2 OpenAPI; scoped-JWT bearer auth.
- **STATUS 2026-08-29 — the standalone service is an ARCHIVED POC.** `entirehq/git-meta-service`
  is read-only ("The real thing is now part of entire-api"). **The supported implementation is
  `entire-api/internal/gitmeta` + `internal/metaengine` + `internal/httpapi/repos_gitmeta.go`** —
  substantial, not a stub. Build clients against that, never the POC.
- **Both former entiredb blockers are RESOLVED** (this section was stale): (a) ADR
  `20260603-reserved-refs` was amended 2026-07-23 to narrow the reservation from all of
  `refs/meta/*` to just `refs/meta/entire/*`, enforcement moved to `refpolicy/refpolicy.go`
  (called at `server/githttp/receive_pack.go:459`); (b) no separate `git-meta` workload is needed —
  `WorkloadEntireAPI` is admitted for entire-api's git-meta receive-pack writes to
  `refs/meta/entire/*` (`svctok_listener.go:419`, ENT-1106). **git-meta can ship, and in
  entire-api it already has.**
- Auth (POC) verified fail-closed **at the binary level** (`go tool nm` links only
  `NotConfiguredAuthenticator`; dev authenticators are all `//go:build gitmeta_dev`, no manifest
  sets the tag). Token repoID is checked against request repoID (403) and pull/push scope is
  enforced per operation (403). entire-api's implementation has **no dev-token path at all**.
- **Two caveats for anything building on it** (e.g. brain fact heads): CAS conflict classification
  rests on **substring-matching go-git/entiredb error text** — flagged fragile in-code, pinned to
  the go.mod version, and it will break silently on a go-git upgrade (typed errors = the durable
  fix). And **CAS-create is NOT a mutual-exclusion primitive**: two writers converging on a
  byte-identical commit BOTH get success, so leader-election use must write a writer-unique value.
- Byte-compatibility with the upstream Rust CLI was **never executed in CI** (golden test `t.Skip`s
  when the CLI is absent, and nothing installed it) — now wired by entire-api **PR #932**, which
  ran green in CI: `git meta 0.1.12`, round-trip tree OID `8a942fee…`. The claim is TRUE, it was
  merely unverified. Trap: `cargo install git-meta` installs the WRONG crate; use **`git-meta-cli`**.
- Local dev: docker-compose Postgres :55432, NATS :54222/:58222. Checkout
  `git-meta-service-gm-heads/` on branch `gm-heads-service` with dirty tree (engine/api/store/
  gitclient edits + untracked `cmd/gitmeta-localtrial`, `cmd/gitmeta-verify`, `cas_test.go`)
  as of 2026-07-16.

# entire-graph — instructions for coding agents (follow directly)

You have a deterministic local code graph: `entire graph` (functions, classes, methods,
types, routes + call/inheritance relations; no network). These instructions are FOR YOU, the
agent reading this file. Use the graph to narrow exploration without trading away correctness.

## The workflow (mandatory for locate/fix/change tasks)

Your FIRST action on any task that requires finding code must be ONE search:

    entire graph search --repo . --profile full --query "<the task or bug in one sentence>"

Then open the top hit's file with your file-read tool (pass a line range around the reported
line), inspect enough surrounding behavior to justify the change, and make the smallest complete
edit. Treat graph output as evidence, not an oracle.

## Hard rules

1. SEARCH FIRST — never grep/find/cat to locate code before you have searched.
2. READ focused source around the result. Widen the check when aliases, generated code, dynamic
   dispatch, or related implementations could matter.
3. Use graph follow-ups only when they answer a real question. For impact or callers, prefer:
       entire graph impact --repo . --symbol X
4. Make the smallest complete edit and check sibling sites or contracts when the task implies them.
5. VERIFY before stopping. Run the most focused relevant test, build, or reproduction available.
   If execution is unavailable, perform a bounded source-level verification and state the limit.
6. Prefer precise queries and line ranges, but never trade resolution for fewer turns.
7. Feature-detect before relying on semantic relations:
       entire graph capabilities --json

## When NOT to use the graph

If the task already names the exact file and it is small, just read it — the graph saves tokens
by eliminating exploration; when there is nothing to explore, skip it.

## Reference

    locate  ->  entire graph search --repo . --profile full --query "..."
    impact  ->  entire graph impact --repo . --symbol X   (one shot: callers, callees, type consumers, data flow, co-change, siblings)
    callers ->  entire graph neighbors --repo . --symbol X --relation CALLS --direction in
    change  ->  entire graph diff --base A --head B --json
    detect  ->  entire graph capabilities --json   (inventory-only languages have no relations)
    stats   ->  entire graph stats --repo .        (human-facing token-savings report; not part of your workflow — do not run it unless asked)

- [Empty-buffer corruption bug](empty-buffer-corruption-bug.md) — checkpoint-on-disk + state-in-memory = 500+ silently wrong answers; audit per-conv latency after ANY resumed run

## 1. What Entire is

Entire wraps AI coding agents (Claude Code, Gemini, OpenCode, Cursor, Factory Droid,
Copilot, Pi) with automatic **session + checkpoint capture**. Agent work is committed as
signed checkpoints to a git-native distributed store, attributed to authors, and surfaced

recaps, and repo dashboards. GitHub-OAuth gated; residency/jurisdiction-aware.

    quorum writes to K-closest, `FindProviders` reads. **No Raft** — correctness from
    content-addressing + Postgres ref CAS + quorum replication.
- **Control plane (`entire-core`)** — identity, OAuth/OIDC, JWKS, SpiceDB authz, repo
  lifecycle. CockroachDB + SpiceDB. `core/identity|authn|authz`, `core/registry|resource|
  repoadmin|provisionerr`, `core/coreapi` (Huma `/api/v1` + login/token), `core/regional|

- `cmd/user-activity` — worker: forwarder consumer → user store.
- Stores (separate pool + Postgres role, no cross-schema joins):

## 11. git-meta-service (detail)

- Implements the [git-meta](https://git-meta.com) exchange format as an API: `(target,key,value)`
  metadata (string/list/set) on commits/branches/paths/change-ids/project, byte-compatible with
  the upstream Rust `git meta` CLI (golden test round-trips vs real CLI if installed).
- **Write path**: serialize → CAS-push to `refs/meta/main` in entiredb (go-git v6 smart HTTP,
  forwards caller's JWT so push authz matches) → materialize into Postgres read-model. Git is
  source of truth; Postgres rebuildable. NATS consumer materializes out-of-band CLI pushes
  (read-only mTLS identity).
- **API** `/api/v1/repos/{repoId}/meta/*`: set/rm, list push/rm, set add/rm, cas (412 precondition /
  409 ref-race), GET query (`target`/`key`/`prefix`). Huma v2 OpenAPI; scoped-JWT bearer auth.
- **STATUS 2026-08-29 — the standalone service is an ARCHIVED POC.** `entirehq/git-meta-service`
  is read-only ("The real thing is now part of entire-api"). **The supported implementation is
  `entire-api/internal/gitmeta` + `internal/metaengine` + `internal/httpapi/repos_gitmeta.go`** —
  substantial, not a stub. Build clients against that, never the POC.
- **Both former entiredb blockers are RESOLVED** (this section was stale): (a) ADR
  `20260603-reserved-refs` was amended 2026-07-23 to narrow the reservation from all of
  `refs/meta/*` to just `refs/meta/entire/*`, enforcement moved to `refpolicy/refpolicy.go`
  (called at `server/githttp/receive_pack.go:459`); (b) no separate `git-meta` workload is needed —
  `WorkloadEntireAPI` is admitted for entire-api's git-meta receive-pack writes to
  `refs/meta/entire/*` (`svctok_listener.go:419`, ENT-1106). **git-meta can ship, and in
  entire-api it already has.**
- Auth (POC) verified fail-closed **at the binary level** (`go tool nm` links only
  `NotConfiguredAuthenticator`; dev authenticators are all `//go:build gitmeta_dev`, no manifest
  sets the tag). Token repoID is checked against request repoID (403) and pull/push scope is
  enforced per operation (403). entire-api's implementation has **no dev-token path at all**.
- **Two caveats for anything building on it** (e.g. brain fact heads): CAS conflict classification
  rests on **substring-matching go-git/entiredb error text** — flagged fragile in-code, pinned to
  the go.mod version, and it will break silently on a go-git upgrade (typed errors = the durable
  fix). And **CAS-create is NOT a mutual-exclusion primitive**: two writers converging on a
  byte-identical commit BOTH get success, so leader-election use must write a writer-unique value.
- Byte-compatibility with the upstream Rust CLI was **never executed in CI** (golden test `t.Skip`s
  when the CLI is absent, and nothing installed it) — now wired by entire-api **PR #932**, which
  ran green in CI: `git meta 0.1.12`, round-trip tree OID `8a942fee…`. The claim is TRUE, it was
  merely unverified. Trap: `cargo install git-meta` installs the WRONG crate; use **`git-meta-cli`**.
- Local dev: docker-compose Postgres :55432, NATS :54222/:58222. Checkout
  `git-meta-service-gm-heads/` on branch `gm-heads-service` with dirty tree (engine/api/store/
  gitclient edits + untracked `cmd/gitmeta-localtrial`, `cmd/gitmeta-verify`, `cas_test.go`)
  as of 2026-07-16.

# entire-graph — instructions for coding agents (follow directly)

You have a deterministic local code graph: `entire graph` (functions, classes, methods,
types, routes + call/inheritance relations; no network). These instructions are FOR YOU, the
agent reading this file. Use the graph to narrow exploration without trading away correctness.

## The workflow (mandatory for locate/fix/change tasks)

Your FIRST action on any task that requires finding code must be ONE search:

    entire graph search --repo . --profile full --query "<the task or bug in one sentence>"

Then open the top hit's file with your file-read tool (pass a line range around the reported
line), inspect enough surrounding behavior to justify the change, and make the smallest complete
edit. Treat graph output as evidence, not an oracle.

## Hard rules

1. SEARCH FIRST — never grep/find/cat to locate code before you have searched.
2. READ focused source around the result. Widen the check when aliases, generated code, dynamic
   dispatch, or related implementations could matter.
3. Use graph follow-ups only when they answer a real question. For impact or callers, prefer:
       entire graph impact --repo . --symbol X
4. Make the smallest complete edit and check sibling sites or contracts when the task implies them.
5. VERIFY before stopping. Run the most focused relevant test, build, or reproduction available.
   If execution is unavailable, perform a bounded source-level verification and state the limit.
6. Prefer precise queries and line ranges, but never trade resolution for fewer turns.
7. Feature-detect before relying on semantic relations:
       entire graph capabilities --json

## When NOT to use the graph

If the task already names the exact file and it is small, just read it — the graph saves tokens
by eliminating exploration; when there is nothing to explore, skip it.

## Reference

    locate  ->  entire graph search --repo . --profile full --query "..."
    impact  ->  entire graph impact --repo . --symbol X   (one shot: callers, callees, type consumers, data flow, co-change, siblings)
    callers ->  entire graph neighbors --repo . --symbol X --relation CALLS --direction in

    detect  ->  entire graph capabilities --json   (inventory-only languages have no relations)

Summary:
1. **Primary Request and Intent:**

   The overarching goal (set via `/goal`, repeatedly evaluated by a stop hook): **"beat all comp on all 12 main gaps; one pr for each viadlte it fully"** — close all 12 REAL GAP rows from `docs/feature-matrix.csv`, one PR per gap, each fully validated.

   - **"don' tmege any prs without my approval - that is invalidl eme0 number dno't update"** — two binding constraints: never merge PRs without explicit approval, and the mem0 benchmark number is invalid and must not be used/published
   - "what is the status on the gaps"
   - "can u not finish all?" — challenge to attempt the remaining two
   - "wait explain to me why we can;t adrees the remauinign 2 gaps"
   - "give the the remainign gap and tell me why u arne;t usign entire grpah uresalf" — caught non-use of entire-graph
   - "give feedback for the entire grpah agent to fix it btw - explaint o me bascialy the gaps || add any other feeddback for grpah int eh ptpmt"
   - "are we losing to a comp on this" (scale row) → "k so then is it a gap?"
   - "k we can hadnel that later wrtei it down in a uncommtied file - don;t shwo to public/push to main"
   - "give a list of all pr fxing gaps and a - next to them sayign what they gap they fix simpel englihs 10 ish to 7ish words" → "k give a cp bullet list of the open ones"
   - "epxain thsi one 0 - #313"
   - "did u use brain to build them btw" → "then acutally sue the stuff we are makign buidl the brain and trhen sue it to help u holy" → "k build the brain"
   - **"distil it - first give me est cost on it - and maek sure u ac use braina dn grpah and u know all abt it and hwo to use it, if it is diff and could be imrpveod then imrpvoe it"** (current task)

2. **Key Technical Concepts:**
   - Entire Gates: 4 sub-gates (Approvals/Checks/Findings/Up-to-date); check name never says which failed; read `output.summary`; completed gates don't re-run — push empty `chore:` commit
   - Trail findings doctrine: "no proof, no fix" (regression test must fail on compile-clean revert); "Default REFUTED"; ~30-40% of findings are stale/refuted/wrong
   - Verified-by-weakening: apply compile-clean weakening, prove the specific test goes red
   - `symbol_fts` is a plain SQLite table (no index) — every search is `instr(lower(text), ?)` full scan
   - FTS5 trigram tokenizer preserves substring semantics but needs LIKE escaping (`%`, `_`, `ESCAPE '\'`)
   - `RUSAGE_SELF` vs `RUSAGE_CHILDREN` for peak RSS
   - Session read guard (`guardFactRecords`/`loadSessionReadGuard`/`blocksFact`) — privacy exclusion
   - Retrieval privacy identity: `captureRetrievalPrivacyPolicy` / `revalidateRetrievalResponsePrivacy` / `writeRetrievalResponseBytes`
   - Content-keyed generation directories (`semantic/generations/<commit>-<digest>/`)
   - Go `map` iteration randomization; `encoding/csv` FieldsPerRecord enforcement
   - `entire brain` verbs: query/search/vsearch search **prose only**; `inspect search-graph`/`inspect code`/`inspect impact` traverse the **symbol graph**
   - Ollama local models (`gemma4:12b`, 262k context, 723 tok/s measured)

3. **Files and Code Sections:**

   - **`/Users/suhaan/devenv/GRAPH-FEEDBACK.md`** (created, UNCOMMITTED, untracked `??`)
     - Field feedback for entire-graph team. §1 intent-query miss rate 1/4; §2 domain-overloaded nouns; §3 cold latency 12.1s; §4 `preselection_confidence: 0.0004` not surfaced; §5 prompt feedback on `.entire/graph-agent.md`; §6 what works; §7 Brain findings appended.
     - Corrected a false claim: originally said team works without brains generally; actually only `entire-brain` lacked one (cli/entiredb/entire.io/entire-api all `manifest: current`; only entire-api has `facts=true`).

   - **`/Users/suhaan/devenv/MATRIX-SCALE-ROW-NOTE.md`** (created, UNCOMMITTED, untracked `??`)
     - Records that the scale row is mis-scored: no competitor rated Yes (mem0/cognee/supermemory all `No`, Graph/Graphify/cmm `Unknown`); the "~100x" is vs Augment which is NOT in the matrix. Three options; recommends option 2 (reword note only). Includes explicit caveat that this reasoning must not be used to claim scale is a win.

   - **`internal/cli/semantic.go`** (#316 branch `perf/verify-once-per-generation`, commit `6775952a`, pushed)
     ```go
     var semanticIntegrityMemo sync.Map
     func fileIdentity(path string) string {
         info, err := os.Stat(path)
         if err != nil { return "missing:" + err.Error() }
         return fmt.Sprintf("%d:%d", info.Size(), info.ModTime().UnixNano())
     }
     func verifiedSnapshotSummary(path, repoKey string) (semanticHeader, semanticCounts, error) {
         key := "snapshot\x00" + path + "\x00" + repoKey + "\x00" + fileIdentity(path)
         ...
     }
     func verifiedSQLiteStore(path string, symbols, relations int) error {
         key := fmt.Sprintf("store\x00%s\x00%d\x00%d\x00%s", path, symbols, relations, fileIdentity(path))
         ...
     }
     ```

   - **`internal/cli/rss_getrusage.go`** (#312, pushed `f7bcaaa9`)
     ```go
     func processMaxRSSBytes() uint64 {
         self := rusageMaxRSSBytes(syscall.RUSAGE_SELF)
         children := rusageMaxRSSBytes(syscall.RUSAGE_CHILDREN)
         return max(self, children)
     }
     ```

   - **`internal/cli/bench_scale.go`** (#312) — `benchIsolatedEnv(env, tempRoot, repoDir)` sets `RepoRoot`; `benchExistingBrainEnv(env, repoDir)` for `--skip-index`; `latencyRuns` only reports when all modes agree; `countFileLines` streams in 64 KiB; refuses `--skip-index` with no index.

   - **`internal/cli/docextract_pdf.go`** (#310) — `pdfMaxPredictorColors = 4`; bpc switch {1,2,4,8,16}; `rowLen > len(data)` bound; per-stream cap re-applied after predictor; `expandPDFObjectStreams(objects, budget)`; `pdfAllToUnicode` returns consumed keys.

   - **`internal/cli/rest_api.go`** (#308, pushed `10243a5d`)
     ```go
     func restGuardedFacts(brainDir, branch string) ([]factRecord, error) {
         facts, err := loadFacts(brainDir, branch)
         manifest, err := loadBrainManifest(brainDir)
         guard, err := loadSessionReadGuard(brainDir, manifest)
         return guardFactRecords(guard, facts), nil
     }
     ```

   - **`internal/cli/facts_import.go`** (#306, pushed `540895bb`) — `countKeptActiveFacts(imported, existing)` extracted and deduped by ID; conflicting-retirement detection; report entry moved outside `!dryRun` branch.

   - **`docs/scale.md`** (#312) — Peak RSS column WITHDRAWN with explanation (72.4 MB vs 203.4 MB, 2.8x); added disclosure that latency includes git subprocess spawns (~30–50 ms).

4. **Errors and fixes:**
   - **Wrote a false claim in a commit message** (#316 said docs/scale.md records the change; that file is on #312's branch) → amended to state it as an unmet requirement.
   - **#316 memo initially weakened integrity** — assumed generations immutable; `TestTheInstantLineDoesNotCallAnUnreadableSemanticIndexBuilt` caught a shredded store reported as built → keyed on size+mtime.
   - **`timeout` doesn't exist on macOS** — two weakening runs silently never executed; nearly reported empty output as OOM evidence → used `go test -timeout` instead.
   - **Three of my own tests passed with the bug present**: (a) RSS test compared process before/after (parent RSS rises anyway) → asserted against children figure directly; (b) CMap budget test computed its ceiling from observed spend → absolute bound from fixture; (c) countFileLines test lacked exact-buffer-multiple cases → added them.
   - **My xlsxSharedStrings "fix" was unreachable code** — read cap bounds at 838,857 < my 1,048,576 ceiling → reverted entirely.
   - **Dry-run fix was half-done** — moved computation out of write branch but left reporting inside → second fix; test fixture also had `replaced_by` inside `metadata` where parser drops it.
   - **Never used entire-graph or entire-brain all session** (user called this out) — direct violation of `.entire/graph-agent.md` ("SEARCH FIRST — never grep/find/cat to locate code before you have searched") and `CLAUDE.md` ("Run `brain_status` first").

# entire-graph — field feedback from a long agent session

Written 2026-09-23 after a full working session in `entire-brain` (~1,800 files,
33 code fixes). Evidence is from this repo, at `gap-scale` @ `1c56dcdf`.

**The headline, and it is uncomfortable: I did not use the graph at all for the
entire session.** Every code location came from `grep`. The repo's own
`.entire/graph-agent.md` says *"SEARCH FIRST — never grep/find/cat to locate
code before you have searched"*, and I violated it on every lookup. That is an
agent-compliance failure first. But when I finally did run it, the results below
explain why nothing pulled me back, and that part is a product problem.

---

## 1. Intent-phrased queries miss; identifier-phrased queries hit

Four queries, each one a lookup I had actually done by grep during the session,
with the correct answer known:

| query | top result | correct | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| "where is peak resident memory measured for the benchmark" | `memoryErrorCode` | `processMaxRSSBytes` | **MISS** (not in top 11) |
| "count lines and bytes of a tracked source file" | `countFileLines` | `countFileLines` | HIT @ 1 |
| "read one part out of an office zip archive with a budget" | `safeReadAll` | `readZipPart` | **MISS** |
| "check the semantic index is fresh before answering a query" | `acquireSemanticIndexLock` | `semanticStaleReport` | **MISS** |

1 / 4. The single hit is the query whose wording happens to echo the
identifier. The three misses are phrased by *intent* — describing what the code
does rather than what it is called.

**This is the central problem, because the prompt asks for intent phrasing.**
`graph-agent.md` says:

> `entire graph search --repo . --profile full --query "<the task or bug in one sentence>"`

A task or bug in one sentence is intent phrasing. The tool is being instructed
to accept exactly the query shape it handles worst.

## 2. Domain-overloaded nouns get captured by the dominant sense

"peak resident **memory**" returned the episodic-**memory** subsystem:
`memoryErrorCode`, `memoryOverlayHealth`, `newMemoryVectorProgressLoadError`,
`loadMemoryConfigChecked`. All eleven results were memory-subsystem symbols.
`rss_getrusage.go` never appeared.

Same failure in the fourth query: "semantic index" matched
`acquireSemanticIndexLock` (locking) rather than `semanticStaleReport`
(freshness), though the query said *fresh*.

In a product whose own feature is called "memory", a query about process memory
is not an exotic edge case. Suggest: when a query term collides with a known
subsystem name, either diversify across senses or surface the ambiguity rather
than silently collapsing to the dominant one.

## 3. Cold latency is high enough to change agent behaviour

    index_cache_hit: false
    index_latency_ms: 9505
    query_latency_ms: 1442
    total_latency_ms: 12103

Twelve seconds on 1,804 files. A grep answers in under one. An agent that tries
the graph once, waits twelve seconds, and gets `memoryErrorCode` for a question
about RSS will not try it a second time — which is precisely what would have
happened to me had I followed the doctrine on day one.

Note this is also the scale problem in miniature: see `docs/scale.md`, where
query latency grows linearly with corpus size.

## 4. `preselection_confidence: 0.0004`

Reported alongside `preselection_widened: true` and `preselection_coverage: 1`.
If that number means what it appears to, the tool already knows this result set
is weak. It is not surfaced to the caller in any actionable way. A result set
the engine has low confidence in should *say so*, so an agent can fall back to
grep deliberately instead of trusting a confident-looking ranked list.

## 5. Feedback on the prompt (`.entire/graph-agent.md`)

The doctrine is well written and I still ignored it, so the prompt has a
compliance problem independent of the engine:

- **It asks for the query shape that performs worst.** Either fix the ranker for
  intent queries, or tell agents to query with likely identifiers and
  domain nouns — "the symbol or term you expect to find", not "the task in one
  sentence".
- **"never grep before you have searched" has no fallback rule.** It says search
  first, but not what to do when the search returns plausible-looking wrong
  answers. That is the common case, and without a stated fallback the agent
  either wastes turns or abandons the tool. Suggest an explicit rule: *if the
  top results do not contain a plausible target, fall back to grep immediately
  and do not retry with a reworded query.*
- **Nothing tells the agent what a bad result looks like.** All four of my
  queries returned eleven confident, well-formatted, completely reasonable
  results. Three were wrong. There is no signal in the output that distinguishes
  "found it" from "here are eleven things that share a word with your query".
  `preselection_confidence` could be that signal.
- **The doctrine is enforced nowhere.** Nothing in the session reminded me, and
  nothing checked. A PreToolUse hook on grep/find that asks whether the graph
  was searched first would have caught me on lookup one. (This is noted as
  built-but-unlaunched in the team's own notes.)

## 6. What works well

Worth saying, because the misses above are the loud part:

- `capabilities --json` is excellent — exhaustive, honest about
  `inventory_only_languages` and `heuristic_relation_types`, and explicit that
  no feature requires network access.
- The result envelope is genuinely good: `signals` explaining *why* something
  ranked, `covering-test` sections, a `verify_command` with its derivation and a
  `tier`, `literal_cluster` with consumer roles, and honest
  `partial_failures` naming minified files it skipped.
- When it hits, it hits at rank 1 with a complete symbol and the test that
  covers it — strictly better than grep for that case.

The engine is not the weak part. The ranking of intent-phrased queries is.

---

## Suggested priority

1. Intent-phrased query ranking (§1) — the doctrine depends on it.
2. Surface low confidence to the caller (§4) — cheap, and turns a silent wrong
   answer into a deliberate fallback.
3. Subsystem-name collision handling (§2).
4. Cold-start latency (§3) — bounded by the scale work already in flight.
5. Prompt changes (§5) — free, and independent of the engine.

---

## 7. Brain: same session, measured after actually building it

I also never used `entire brain` during the session. Unlike the graph, it had
nothing to give — but I did not know that, because I never ran the check that
would have told me.

**The brain was not built for this repo.** `manifest: absent`, every source
`false`, in the main checkout and in both worktrees I tried. One `entire brain
refresh` fixed it in about a minute.

Corrected after checking the other checkouts — the first draft of this note said
the team were working without brains generally, and that is not true:

| repo | seed | sessions | semantic | history | facts | docs |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| entire-brain | (absent until I built it) | | | | | |
| cli | yes | yes | yes | yes | **no** | yes |
| entiredb | no | yes | yes | yes | **no** | no |
| entire.io | no | yes | yes | yes | **no** | no |
| entire-api | yes | yes | yes | yes | **yes** | no |

Every other core repo had a current brain. The one repo without one was the
brain's own. That is a narrower point than I first wrote, and a more pointed
one.

**`facts` is false in four of five.** `entire-api` is the only repo with a
distilled facts layer. That is the layer carrying "we tried X and it was
refuted" — the thing that would have saved the most time this session — and it
is empty almost everywhere because `distill` is agent-gated and nobody pays
that cost routinely.

`CLAUDE.md` says *"Run `brain_status` first — it reports whether facts/semantic
are built for the repo you're in."* That step exists precisely to answer this in
one call, and skipping it is how an agent ends up assuming instead of checking.
Worth making it harder to skip.

### After building it — what helped

- `inspect code "peak resident memory rss"` → `rss_children_test.go` at rank 1.
  Right file family. The graph gave `memoryErrorCode` for the same question.
- `brief` → `likely_edit_files` led with `bench_scale.go`, `likely_test_files`
  with `bench_scale_test.go`. For benchmark work, the right area on the first
  call.
- The `guidance` block is good, and honest: *"Treat the brain as an indexed
  snapshot, not live memory"*, *"Use the live-state overlay before trusting
  semantic results for files changed in this session."*

### After building it — what did not

- **`brief` returned `semantic hits: 0`** despite `semantic=true` and a healthy
  store (`snapshot: ok`, `store: ok`). A brief whose semantic section is empty
  on a built brain looks like a bug.
- **`history matches: 3`, all with empty text.** Three matches that carry
  nothing readable.
- **`brief` pointed at the benchmark, not the implementation.** The task named
  "query latency in the semantic index"; the work lives in `semantic.go`, and
  `likely_edit_files` led with `bench_scale.go`. Adjacent, not the target.
- **`query` for the RSS question returned docs, not code** —
  `release_press_release.md`, `testing-for-optimization.md`. Same
  overloaded-noun failure as the graph (§2), different surface.
- **`facts=false` after a fresh refresh.** `distill` is agent-gated, so the
  durable-facts layer — the part most likely to carry "we tried X and it was
  refuted" — is empty by default. That is the layer that would have saved me
  the most this session, and a new brain does not have it.
- `semantic_completeness: degraded (45 partial failures)` — minified JSON under
  `benchmarks/`. Expected, but it is the default state of this repo's own brain.

### The honest counterfactual

Had I followed the doctrine on day one: `brain status` would have said "absent"
in one call, `refresh` would have built it in a minute, and `brief` would have
put me in `bench_scale.go` on my first lookup instead of my third grep. It would
**not** have found `processMaxRSSBytes` or `semanticStaleReport` — the two
findings that mattered most this session.

So the tools would have helped, partially, and I should have used them. Neither
would have found the session's best results. Both facts belong in the same
sentence.

# Scale row is mis-scored — decide before #315 merges

**Status: internal note. Not committed, not pushed, not for publication.**
Written 2026-09-23. Decision deferred by user.

## What the data says

`docs/feature-matrix.csv`, row "Scales to 100M-line codebases":

| | |
|---|---|
| Entire Brain | No |
| mem0 | No |
| cognee | No |
| supermemory | No |
| Entire Graph | Unknown |
| Graphify | Unknown |
| codebase-memory-mcp | Unknown |

**No competitor in the table is rated Yes.** Three rated `No`, two `Unknown`.

## The problem

deficit*. It is not one. Nobody in the comparison set does this.

source column (`augmentcode.com/blog/repo-scale-100M-line-codebase-quantized-vector-search`).
Augment is **not a column in this matrix**. It is an outside reference.

My note then compounded it by writing *"Now MEASURED and a loss"*, which reads
as losing to the field. Against the field we are tied at `No`, and we are the
only entry whose `No` is measured rather than asserted.

- **Product limitation** — is there a real ceiling users hit? **Yes.** 1.17 GB

  regardless of what competitors do.

   misleading — invites the reading that competitors do this and we do not.

   table scales to 100M lines, that we are the only measured entry, and that
   Augment is an outside reference. Touches no number.

   competitive gap. This changes what "12 gaps" means and is a judgement about

distrusted. **Scale is not a win.** The product limitation is real, five

name: semantic-fts5-trigram-refuted
description: FTS5 trigram on symbol_fts is 2.2x SLOWER on real queries and 18x slower to build — measured and refuted 2026-09-22; scale stays a loss
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 6ca2c8fb-c97b-4bf3-a992-0e3c6d1967e2
  modified: 2026-09-22T22:51:55.344Z
---

`symbol_fts` really is a **plain table with no index** (`CREATE TABLE symbol_fts (id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, text TEXT NOT NULL)`), and every search is `instr(lower(text), ?)` over every row. A phrase query costs one full scan for the verbatim match **plus one more scan per token** for document frequency (`semantic.go` ~:4388). That mechanism is real and explains the linear latency in [[brain-does-not-scale-past-5m-lines]] — 299 ms at 174k lines to 12.3 s at 4.8M is ~2.6 ms/kloc throughout.

**The obvious fix — FTS5 with `tokenize='trigram'` and indexed `LIKE` — is REFUTED by measurement.** Built it, ran `bench scale` with both binaries on the same clean 747k-line corpus (50,240 symbols), 24 samples per arm:

| | scan | trigram |
|---|---|---|
| code_search p50 | 1,223 ms | 2,679 ms (**0.46x**) |
| index build | 17.0 s | 309.7 s (**18x**) |
| index size | 202 MB | 232 MB (1.15x) |

**Why**, and this is the reusable part: trigram only wins on *selective* terms. Synthetic probes on the same build gave **40x** for a token matching 150/150k rows, **0.3x** for one matching every row. The benchmark's natural-language queries ("how is the cache invalidated") tokenize to `error`, `configuration`, `handling` — common in any codebase, so non-selective, so the index loses. Trigram also indexes every 3-char window, hence the build cost.

Correctness notes if anyone retries: trigram + `LIKE` **does** reproduce `instr` semantics exactly (verified identical result sets, including non-token-boundary substrings and dotted terms) — but `LIKE` gives `%`/`_` wildcard meaning that `instr` never did, so every argument needs escaping plus `ESCAPE '\'`. The repo's own `TestSemanticQueryTreatsSQLiteSearchTextLiterally` catches that regression.

**How to apply:** don't re-propose trigram. If scale is attacked again, the lever is query *selectivity* (IDF-gate the tokens before touching the store, or a real inverted index with postings-list intersection), not swapping the matcher. And measure on a real corpus with the real query set — two of my three synthetic probes gave the wrong answer because the fixture decided the result. See [[verified-by-weakening-doctrine]].

Branch `perf/semantic-fts5` in `gap-fts` holds the working implementation, unpushed, if the numbers are ever worth re-deriving.

Closed all 12 REAL GAP rows from `docs/feature-matrix.csv`, one PR per gap, 2026-09-21/22. **Only #303 merged; the rest await human approval — never self-approve.**

entire-brain: #303 brain_remember (MERGED) · #304 recency · #305 plain files · #306 mem0 import · #307 HTTP MCP · #308 REST+SDKs · #309 webhooks · #310 PDF/Office ingest · #311 global facts · #312 scale benchmark · #313 published benchmarks (stacked on #312) · #314 README install prose · **#315 consolidated matrix re-score**.
entire-graph: #264 edge provenance.

**Zero open findings across all 10 trails after 13 rounds:** 44 dispositioned, 31 confirmed+fixed, 13 refuted (~30%). Gates read Checks/Findings/Up-to-date green with only Approvals red.

**The 2026-09-22 round found two real defects in my own work that reasoning alone would have missed:**
- **#308**: REST wrote search results under the *pre-ranking* privacy identity while every other surface uses the post-revalidation one. A cleanly-completed concurrent exclusion then made the write boundary refuse rows it had already filtered — surfacing as **HTTP 200 with an empty body**, because the status line is written before the body. Availability bug, not a leak (it failed closed).
- **#311**: merging global facts into the ranked set put them in front of per-repo semantic caches keyed by `(brainDir, branch)`. `recall`'s existing guard filtered only `retain` — but `factVector` caches *and* marks touched during ranking, so it was half a guard and copying it would have copied the hole. Fixed at the reranker (`markForeign`), now shared by recall/query/search/vsearch/brief.

**Global facts were CLI-recall-only until #311's second round:** `mergeGlobalFacts` had exactly one caller. `brain_remember` had no `global` argument at all, so the MCP agent — the primary consumer — could neither write nor read one. Also: merging inside brief's `status.Sources.Facts` gate was wrong; a repo with no facts of its own is precisely the case global facts exist for, so the load must be hoisted above the gate.

**Two gaps are honest losses, recorded as such in #315 rather than rounded up:** scale (see [[brain-does-not-scale-past-5m-lines]]) and published benchmarks (Partial — the page exists but is still not a head-to-head; manufacturing one would trip the repo's own `no_release_claim` auditor).

**How to apply:** don't quote a gap as closed until its PR merges. #315 must merge LAST — its rows describe what the others ship. Resolving findings does NOT re-run a completed gate; push an empty `chore:` commit. See [[verified-by-weakening-doctrine]] — it caught ~10 unfailable tests here, including two I wrote this round (a source-grep test and a widened branch no data exercised).
