entries.name: Monitor
entries.description:
Start a background monitor that streams events from a long-running script. Each stdout line is an event — you keep working and notifications arrive in the chat. Events arrive on their own schedule and are not replies from the user, even if one lands while you're waiting for the user to answer a question.

Pick by how many notifications you need:
- **One** ("tell me when the server is ready / the build finishes") → use **Bash with `run_in_background`** and a command that exits when the condition is true, e.g. `until grep -q "Ready in" dev.log; do sleep 0.5; done`. You get a single completion notification when it exits.
- **One per occurrence, until the monitor expires (re-arm to continue)** ("tell me every time an ERROR line appears") → Monitor with an unbounded command (`tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, `while true`).
- **One per occurrence, until a known end** ("emit each CI step result, stop when the run completes") → Monitor with a command that emits lines and then exits.

Your script's stdout is the event stream. Each line becomes a notification. Exit ends the watch.

  # Each matching log line is an event
  tail -f /var/log/app.log | grep --line-buffered "ERROR"

  # Each file change is an event
  inotifywait -m --format '%e %f' /watched/dir

  # Poll GitHub for new PR comments and emit one line per new comment
  last=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
  while true; do
    now=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
    gh api "repos/owner/repo/issues/123/comments?since=$last" --jq '.[] | "\(.user.login): \(.body)"'
    last=$now; sleep 30
  done

  # Node script that emits events as they arrive (e.g. WebSocket listener)
  node watch-for-events.js

  # Per-occurrence with a natural end: emit each CI check as it lands, exit when the run completes
  prev=""
  while true; do
    s=$(gh pr checks 123 --json name,bucket)
    cur=$(jq -r '.[] | select(.bucket!="pending") | "\(.name): \(.bucket)"' <<<"$s" | sort)
    comm -13 <(echo "$prev") <(echo "$cur")
    prev=$cur
    jq -e 'all(.bucket!="pending")' <<<"$s" >/dev/null && break
    sleep 30
  done

**Don't use an unbounded command for a single notification.** `tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, and `while true` never exit on their own, so the monitor stays armed until timeout even after the event has fired. For "tell me when X is ready," use Bash `run_in_background` with an `until` loop instead (one notification, ends in seconds). Note that `tail -f log | grep -m 1 ...` does *not* fix this: if the log goes quiet after the match, `tail` never receives SIGPIPE and the pipeline hangs anyway.

**Script quality:**
- Every pipe stage must flush per line or matches sit in its buffer unseen: `grep` needs `--line-buffered`, `awk` needs `fflush()`. `head` cannot flush at all — `| head -N` delivers nothing until N matches accumulate, then ends the stream.
- In poll loops, handle transient failures (`curl ... || true`) — one failed request shouldn't kill the monitor.
- Poll intervals: 30s+ for remote APIs (rate limits), 0.5-1s for local checks.
- Write a specific `description` — it appears in every notification ("errors in deploy.log" not "watching logs").
- Only stdout is the event stream. Stderr goes to the output file (readable via Read) but does not trigger notifications — for a command you run directly (e.g. `python train.py 2>&1 | grep --line-buffered ...`), merge stderr with `2>&1` so its failures reach your filter. (No effect on `tail -f` of an existing log — that file only contains what its writer redirected.)

**Coverage — silence is not success.** When watching a job or process for an outcome, your filter must match every terminal state, not just the happy path. A monitor that greps only for the success marker stays silent through a crashloop, a hung process, or an unexpected exit — and silence looks identical to "still running." Before arming, ask: *if this process crashed right now, would my filter emit anything?* If not, widen it.

  # Wrong — silent on crash, hang, or any non-success exit
  tail -f run.log | grep --line-buffered "elapsed_steps="

  # Right — one alternation covering progress + the failure signatures you'd act on
  tail -f run.log | grep -E --line-buffered "elapsed_steps=|Traceback|Error|FAILED|assert|Killed|OOM"

For poll loops checking job state, emit on every terminal status (`succeeded|failed|cancelled|timeout`), not just success. If you cannot confidently enumerate the failure signatures, broaden the grep alternation rather than narrow it — some extra noise is better than missing a crashloop.

**Output volume**: Every stdout line is a conversation message, so the filter should be selective — but selective means "the lines you'd act on," not "only good news." Never pipe raw logs; filter to exactly the success and failure signals you care about. Monitors that produce too many events are automatically stopped; restart with a tighter filter if this happens.

Stdout lines within 200ms are batched into a single notification, so multiline output from a single event groups naturally.

The script runs in the same shell environment as Bash. Exit ends the watch (exit code is reported). Every monitor expires after `timeout_ms` (default 5 minutes, at most 30 minutes): it is killed and you get one notice with the event count. Re-arm it if you still need the watch; for a long watch (PR monitoring, log tails) set `timeout_ms` to the maximum and re-arm on each expiry, and widen the filter if an expiry with no events was unexpected. Use TaskStop to cancel early.
**ws source** — open a WebSocket and stream each incoming text frame as an event. No shell, no polling: the server pushes, you get notified.

  Monitor({
    ws: {url: 'wss://events.example.com/stream', protocols: ['v1']},
    description: 'deploy events',
  })

Each text frame becomes one notification (multiline frames stay as one event). Binary frames are reported as `[binary frame, N bytes]` rather than passed through. Socket close ends the watch with the close code surfaced; errors are surfaced before close. Same rate limiting as bash — a firehose will be suppressed and eventually stopped, so subscribe to a filtered feed where one exists.

Prefer this over `command: 'websocat wss://…'` — it avoids the extra process and line-buffering pitfalls. Use bash when you need to transform or filter frames with shell tools before they become events.

When an event lands that the user would want to act on now — an error appeared, the status they were waiting on flipped — send a PushNotification. Not every event is worth a push; the ones that change what they'd do next are.

description.description: Short human-readable description of what you are monitoring (shown in notifications).

timeout_ms.description: Kill the monitor after this deadline. Default 300000ms. Deadlines above 1800000ms are capped to 1800000ms. You are notified at expiry and can re-arm.

command.description: Shell command or script. Each stdout line is an event; exit ends the watch.

ws.description: WebSocket to open. Each text frame is an event; binary frames are reported as a placeholder line. Socket close ends the watch. Cannot be combined with command.

entries.name: TaskList
entries.description:
Use this tool to list all tasks in the task list.

## When to Use This Tool

- To see what tasks are available to work on (status: 'pending', no owner, not blocked)
- To check overall progress on the project
- To find tasks that are blocked and need dependencies resolved
- After completing a task, to check for newly unblocked work or claim the next available task
- **Prefer working on tasks in ID order** (lowest ID first) when multiple tasks are available, as earlier tasks often set up context for later ones

## Output

Returns a summary of each task:
- **id**: Task identifier (use with TaskGet, TaskUpdate)
- **subject**: Brief description of the task
- **status**: 'pending', 'in_progress', or 'completed'
- **owner**: Agent ID if assigned, empty if available
- **blockedBy**: List of open task IDs that must be resolved first (tasks with blockedBy cannot be claimed until dependencies resolve)

Use TaskGet with a specific task ID to view full details including description and comments.

entries.name: TaskStop
entries.description:
- Stops a running background task by its ID
- Takes a task_id parameter identifying the task to stop
- To stop an agent-team teammate, pass its agent ID ("name@team") or bare teammate name as task_id
- To stop a background agent spawned with a name, pass that name as task_id
- Returns a success or failure status
- Use this tool when you need to terminate a long-running task

task_id.description: The ID of the background task to stop. Agent-team teammates and named background agents are also accepted by agent ID or name.

entries.name: WebFetch
entries.description:
Fetches a URL, converts the page to markdown, and answers `prompt` against it using a small fast model.

- Fails on authenticated/private URLs — use an authenticated MCP tool or `gh` for those instead. Exception: claude.ai artifact links (claude.ai/artifact/{id} or claude.ai/code/artifact/{uuid}) ARE fetchable via your claude.ai login — use WebFetch, not curl (curl gets the SPA shell or a Cloudflare 403).
- Fails on localhost and other hostnames without a dot; for a local server, use curl via Bash.
- HTTP is upgraded to HTTPS. Cross-host redirects are returned to you rather than followed; call again with the redirect URL.
- Responses are cached for 15 minutes per URL.

prompt.description: The prompt to run on the fetched content

entries.description:
Search the web. Returns result blocks with titles and URLs. US-only.

- After answering from results, end with a "Sources:" list of the URLs you used as markdown links.

entries.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__computer
entries.description:
Use a mouse and keyboard to interact with a web browser, and take screenshots. If you don't have a valid tab ID, use tabs_context_mcp first to get available tabs.
* Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element before moving the cursor.
* If you tried clicking on a program or link but it failed to load, even after waiting, try adjusting your click location so that the tip of the cursor visually falls on the element that you want to click.
* Make sure to click any buttons, links, icons, etc with the cursor tip in the center of the element. Don't click boxes on their edges unless asked.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported and will return an error - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels. Requires a Claude in Chrome extension version that supports scale; older extensions return the full-size image.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

tabId.description: Tab ID to execute the action on. Must be a tab in the current group. Use tabs_context_mcp first if you don't have a valid tab ID.

save_to_disk.description: For screenshot/zoom actions: save the image to disk so it can be attached to a message for the user. Returns the saved path in the tool result. Only set this when you intend to share the image — screenshots you're just looking at don't need saving.

entries.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__javascript_tool
entries.description: Execute JavaScript code in the context of the current page. The code runs in the page's context and can interact with the DOM, window object, and page variables. Returns the result of the last expression or any thrown errors. If you don't have a valid tab ID, use tabs_context_mcp first to get available tabs.

text.description: The JavaScript code to execute. Evaluated in the page context with REPL semantics: top-level `await` works, and the result of the last expression is returned automatically — write the expression you want (e.g. `window.myData.value`, or `await fetch(url).then(r=>r.json())`) rather than `return ...`. You can access and modify the DOM, call page functions, and interact with page variables.

tabId.description: Tab ID to execute the code in. Must be a tab in the current group. Use tabs_context_mcp first if you don't have a valid tab ID.

entries.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__navigate
entries.description: Navigate to a URL, or go forward/back in browser history. tabId may be omitted for URL navigation when calling navigate STANDALONE (not inside browser_batch): tabs_context_mcp{createIfEmpty:true} is called for you and the first tab in the session's group is navigated — its result is appended to this call's output so you have the tab list and ids for subsequent calls. Inside browser_batch, navigate (and other tools that act on a page) requires an explicit tabId. Pass an explicit tabId when you need a specific tab or when the session's group has multiple tabs whose state you must preserve. tabId is required for url:"back"/"forward". A tab opened for you this way is yours to clean up, the same as one from tabs_create_mcp: close it with tabs_close_mcp once you no longer need it and before finishing your task, unless the user asked to see it or wants it kept open.

url.description: The URL to navigate to. Can be provided with or without protocol (defaults to https://). Use "forward" to go forward in history or "back" to go back in history.

tabId.description: Tab ID to navigate. Must be a tab in the current group. If omitted for URL navigation when calling navigate standalone, tabs_context_mcp{createIfEmpty:true} is called for you. Required for url:"back"/"forward" and for navigate (and other tools that act on a page) inside browser_batch.

entries.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__resize_window
entries.description: Resize the current browser window to specified dimensions. Useful for testing responsive designs or setting up specific screen sizes. If you don't have a valid tab ID, use tabs_context_mcp first to get available tabs.

tabId.description: Tab ID to get the window for. Must be a tab in the current group. Use tabs_context_mcp first if you don't have a valid tab ID.

entries.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_close_mcp
entries.description: Close a tab in the MCP tab group by its ID. Use to clean up tabs you're done with. Only tabs in this session's group are closable; call tabs_context_mcp first to get valid IDs. If you close the group's last tab, Chrome auto-removes the group — the next tabs_context_mcp with createIfEmpty starts fresh.

tabId.description: The ID of the tab to close. Must be in this session's tab group. Get valid IDs from tabs_context_mcp.

entries.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp
entries.description: Get context information about the current MCP tab group. Returns all tab IDs inside the group if it exists. CRITICAL: You must get the context at least once before using other browser automation tools so you know what tabs exist. Each new conversation should create its own new tab (using tabs_create_mcp) rather than reusing existing tabs, unless the user explicitly asks to use an existing tab.

createIfEmpty.description: Creates a new MCP tab group if none exists, creates a new Window with a new tab group containing an empty tab (which can be used for this conversation). If a MCP tab group already exists, this parameter has no effect.

entries.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp
entries.description: Creates a new empty tab in the MCP tab group. CRITICAL: You must get the context using tabs_context_mcp at least once before using other browser automation tools so you know what tabs exist. Tabs you create are yours to clean up: close each one with tabs_close_mcp as soon as you no longer need it, and close any that remain before finishing your task. Leave a tab open only if the user asked to see it or wants it kept open.

### [2026-09-11] session (video/repro) → graph-bench · FINDING
FAIR20 is asymmetric AGAINST eg — baseline got BASE_CLAMP, eg got nothing to replace the shared block

Isolated on astral-sh__ruff-15309, where BOTH cells ran claude-opus-5 on BOTH arms, so model is
controlled. Prompt-marker audit:

  cell/arm            words  shared-11-rule-block  BASE_CLAMP
  ONeg_r2      eg       781          YES               no
  ONbaseline_r2 base    622          YES               no      <- symmetric, eg +64.8%
  FAIR20       eg       504          NO                no
  FAIR20       base     304          NO               YES      <- asymmetric, eg -216.1%

In FAIR20 the tool-agnostic "How to work (this applies whatever tools you use)" block is absent
from BOTH arms, but baseline alone was handed BASE_CLAMP in its place. So baseline kept explicit
efficiency discipline ("ONE batched search ... minimal edit, STOP") while eg kept none: it lost
r7 batch-into-one-call, r9 at-most-ONE-verification/never-loop-edit-run-edit, r10 all-edits-in-one-
message, r11 no-narration. BASE_CLAMP's content passes the "would this help an arm with no tool?"
test in the eg direction too, so giving it to one arm only is the same instruction-class defect
that killed 54.9% and 31.6% — just pointing the other way.

Consequence is visible in the turn counts on that identical instance/model: eg 8 -> 40 turns,
baseline 27 -> 15. eg's 5x turn blowup is what the pooled -188.5% is made of.

So FAIR20's -188.5% is NOT the honest number any more than the old defective cells' +71% was.
A clean cell needs the SAME discipline text on both arms (either the 11-rule shared block on both,
as ON/FS/NH/KH/PF/SF/DS/SN/FR/FF/DH/LS did, or BASE_CLAMP plus its eg-analogue on both).

Cross-checked the 47 winners from the July cells: 47/47 same model both arms, 47/47 exactly one
prompt diff hunk (tool block only), 47/47 shared block symmetric (35 present-both, 12 absent-both),
length ratio 1.03-1.26. 3 of them (lombok-3042, faker-2705, prometheus-10633) had ZERO eg tool
calls and are dropped as not attributable. The other 44 stand as fair.

content.text:
Confirmed — and it's worse than a missing flag. On `main` the CLI says *"all captured sessions are distilled — the answer may genuinely not be in the brain"* while those 4 facts sit one branch away. The reassurance steers you away from data that exists.

That matters structurally: sessions happen on feature branches, so distilled facts land there, while agents work on `main`. **The default view is the empty one.**

input.command:
cd /Users/suhaan/devenv
cat >> GRAPH-FEEDBACK.md <<'EOF'

---

## 8. Brain: the distill path, measured by actually running it

Added 2026-09-23 after building the facts layer for `entire-brain` end to end. §7 said
`facts=false` in four of five repos and blamed cost. Having now paid the cost, the reason is
more specific, and one part of it is a defect.

### 8.1 The ollama output cap measures the wrong bytes (defect — fixed)

`distill --agent ollama` failed with `ollama output exceeds 262144 bytes` on chunks the model
answered in **two bytes**. The cap is applied to the raw HTTP body, and `/api/generate` echoes
a `context` token array proportional to the *prompt*:

| prompt | envelope | generated text | `context` |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2 KB | 5,731 B | **2 B** | 1,092 ints (~6.5 KB) |
| 48 KB | 123,468 B | **2 B** | 24,640 ints (~148 KB) |

The distiller never reads `context`. Consequences: `--max-chunk-bytes` is silently ceilinged at
roughly 96 KB for the ollama agent; past that every chunk fails; and the error blames output the
model never produced, so the obvious remedy (lower the chunk size) is discoverable only by
reading the source. I lost a 9-minute validation run to it before finding the cause.

Fixed on `fix/ollama-envelope-limit`: bound the envelope proportionally to the request we
control, and cap the decoded `response` at `distillMaxOutputBytes` with a message that names it.
Two regression tests, each verified red on a compile-clean revert.

### 8.2 The free local path does not pay off

Measured on one real 306 KB session with `gemma4:12b`:

    535 s  ->  4 facts, with a flood of "dropped line without tab separator"

Extrapolated to the 16.5 MB corpus: ~8 hours for ~215 facts. The drops are the real problem —
the prompt asks for `kind<TAB>path<TAB>fact` and the model answers in markdown prose, so most of
what it generates is discarded after being paid for. A 12B local model does not hold the output
contract over long chunks.

The four facts it *did* produce are good, and are exactly the class §7 predicted would help most:

> A semantic floor for Model2Vec on history was tried and rejected: low-variance cosine scores
> on long prose (avg ~0.2) made it impossible to distinguish relevant content from noise.

One is subtly corrupted — "Facts BM2S" for BM25 — which is worth noting because a fact store is
read as authoritative and nothing downstream re-checks a distilled string against its source.

Suggestion: the drop rate is already computed (every drop is a warning). Surface it as a summary
statistic and fail loudly when it crosses some threshold, rather than emitting hundreds of
individually-plausible warnings. A run that discards 90% of what it generated should say so in
one line.

### 8.3 Facts are branch-scoped, and the default view is the empty one

The distilled facts landed on `feat/stage1a-derived-index` — the branch the session ran on. On
`main`:

    $ entire brain recall "model2vec semantic floor"
    no facts for "model2vec semantic floor" on main
    note: facts last distilled 2026-09-23 and all captured sessions are distilled
          — the answer may genuinely not be in the brain

    $ entire brain recall --branch feat/stage1a-derived-index
    fact:4d5bedfd... closed-negative  A semantic floor for Model2Vec ...   (+3 more)

**The note is confidently wrong.** It asserts the answer is genuinely absent while the fact sits
one branch away, and it does so in exactly the reassuring register that stops an agent looking
further. This is not a rare corner: sessions are recorded on feature branches, so that is where
distilled facts land, while agents mostly work on `main`. The default view will usually be empty.

Minimum fix: when a branch-scoped recall finds nothing, count the facts on other branches and say
so — "0 on main, 4 on 2 other branches; try --branch" — instead of reassuring the caller that the
corpus is exhausted. Better: make cross-branch recall the default for `closed-negative` and
`decision` kinds, which are rarely branch-specific in the way code is.

### 8.4 The prose/symbol split is the thing I most needed told

`query`, `search` and `vsearch` search **prose only**. Searching a Go identifier returns docs:

    $ entire brain search "processMaxRSSBytes"     -> seed/history-gaps.md
    $ entire brain inspect search-graph processMaxRSSBytes
      processMaxRSSBytes   internal/cli/rss_getrusage.go

`inspect search-graph` found both symbols that `entire graph search` missed in §1
(`processMaxRSSBytes`, `semanticStaleReport`). So the capability I spent §1 complaining was
absent *does exist* — under a different verb, on a different tool, and I found it only by
reading `brain guide` end to end.

That is the single highest-value correction in this document. `graph-agent.md` should say plainly:
**prose verbs and symbol verbs are different; for an identifier use `inspect search-graph`.**

### 8.5 A brain built in a worktree is stale everywhere else

    freshness: unsafe   branch_tip: stale   current: main   indexed: feat/scale-benchmark

One repo-key is shared across every worktree, so a brain built in one is stale for all the
others. With the clone-per-task doctrine this repo actually follows, that is the normal state,
not the exception. `refresh` fixes it in about a minute, but nothing prompts you to.
EOF

cd /Users/suhaan/devenv/brain-ollama-envelope
gh pr create --repo entireio/entire-brain --base main --head fix/ollama-envelope-limit \
 --title "fix(distill): bound the ollama envelope, not the generated text" \
 --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
## The defect

`distill --agent ollama` capped the raw HTTP response body at `distillMaxOutputBytes` (256 KiB). But `/api/generate` echoes a `context` token array proportional to the **prompt**, and the distiller never reads it — so the cap measured prompt size, not output size.

Measured against a local `gemma4:12b`, with the model replying `ok` both times:

| prompt | envelope | generated text | echoed `context` |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2 KB | 5,731 B | **2 B** | 1,092 ints (~6.5 KB) |
| 48 KB | 123,468 B | **2 B** | 24,640 ints (~148 KB) |

The envelope runs ~2.5x the prompt. So `--max-chunk-bytes` was silently ceilinged near 96 KB for this agent, and past that *every* chunk failed with:

```
ollama output exceeds 262144 bytes
```

That message names output the model never produced. Anyone debugging it reaches for the generation knobs; the actual cause is the chunk size, discoverable only by reading the source. I lost a validation run to exactly this before finding it.

## The fix

Bound the envelope read proportionally to the request we control, and keep `distillMaxOutputBytes` as the cap on the decoded `response`, where the name is accurate.

Both limits are still enforced. Neither is now a function of how much prompt we sent. The factor is 8x with 64 KiB of slack against a measured ~3x worst case for dense ASCII, so there is headroom for tokenizers that split finer.

## Verification

Two regression tests, each **verified red on a compile-clean revert** — not merely passing:

- restoring the old envelope bound fails the accept test with the real-world symptom: `envelope of 294072 bytes carrying 43 bytes of generated text must be accepted`
- deleting the response cap fails the reject test: `generated text over distillMaxOutputBytes must be rejected`

Full `internal/cli` package green (249s, exit 0).

## Note for reviewers

This is one of three problems found in the ollama distill path while building this repo's own facts layer. The other two are **not** addressed here and want their own changes:

1. **Silent prompt truncation.** The request sends no `options`, so ollama loads gemma4 at `num_ctx: 32768`. A 48 KB chunk is at or past that, and ollama truncates the prompt rather than erroring — so the model distills part of a chunk and nothing says so. Currently being measured.
2. **Output-contract drift.** A 12B local model answers in markdown prose instead of `kind<TAB>path<TAB>fact`, so most generated text is discarded via `dropped line without tab separator` after being paid for. The drop rate is already computed per-line; it should be surfaced as one summary statistic rather than hundreds of individually-plausible warnings.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
EOF
)" 2>&1 | tail -3

---
name: brain-prose-vs-symbol-verbs
description: brain query/search/vsearch search PROSE only; inspect search-graph is the symbol tool and found symbols entire-graph search missed
metadata:
  type: reference
---

`entire brain` has two disjoint search surfaces and nothing in the CLI says so:

- **prose** — `query`, `search`, `vsearch`, `recall` search docs/history/facts. Searching a Go
  identifier returns markdown: `search "processMaxRSSBytes"` → `seed/history-gaps.md`.
- **symbols** — `inspect search-graph`, `inspect code`, `inspect impact` traverse the code graph.
  `inspect search-graph processMaxRSSBytes` → `internal/cli/rss_getrusage.go`, first hit.

This matters because `inspect search-graph` found **both** symbols that `entire graph search`
missed on intent-phrased queries (`processMaxRSSBytes`, `semanticStaleReport`) — see
[[entire-graph-intent-query-miss]] if written. The capability I spent a feedback doc calling
absent does exist, under a different verb on a different tool.

Also: `inspect impact <symbol>` returns `roots`/`symbols`/`relations` — the blast radius, one call.

**How to apply:** identifier or symbol → `inspect search-graph`. Intent or "why did we…" →
`query`/`recall`. Never conclude a symbol is absent from a prose verb's empty result.

Two workflow traps: a brain built in one worktree reports `freshness: unsafe` for every other
worktree sharing the repo-key (one `refresh` per branch fixes it), and facts are **branch-scoped**
— see [[brain-facts-are-branch-scoped]].
EOF

cat > $M/brain-facts-are-branch-scoped.md <<'EOF'
---
name: brain-facts-are-branch-scoped
description: distilled facts land on the session's feature branch, so recall on main is empty AND tells you the corpus is exhausted — a confidently wrong note
metadata:
  type: reference
---

Distilled facts are stored per branch, under the branch the *session* ran on. Sessions run on
feature branches; agents work on `main`. So the default view is usually the empty one.

    $ entire brain recall "model2vec semantic floor"
    no facts for "model2vec semantic floor" on main
    note: facts last distilled 2026-09-23 and all captured sessions are distilled
          — the answer may genuinely not be in the brain      <-- FALSE

    $ entire brain recall --branch feat/stage1a-derived-index
    fact:4d5bedfd... closed-negative  A semantic floor for Model2Vec was tried and rejected...

The note is the damaging part: it asserts absence, in a reassuring register, while the fact sits
one branch away. `emptyResultBlindSpot` in `internal/cli/blind_spot.go` already checks store
integrity and distill coverage before saying this — it just never checks other branches.

**How to apply:** an empty `recall` on main proves nothing. Check
`entire brain status --json | .facts.branches` and retry with `--branch`, or enumerate stores under
`~/.local/share/entire/plugins/data/brain/repos/<repo-key>/facts/`. The brain is NOT in the repo's
`.entire/` — looking there and finding nothing is how I first concluded zero facts existed when
four did. See [[brain-prose-vs-symbol-verbs]].
EOF

cat > $M/ollama-distill-economics.md <<'EOF'
---
name: ollama-distill-economics
description: local gemma4:12b distill is ~8h/$0 for entire-brain's 203 sessions; three defects in the ollama path, two fixed in brain PR #317
metadata:
  type: project
---

Measured 2026-09-23 building entire-brain's own facts layer (it was the one repo of five with
`facts=false`).

**Corpus:** 203 sessions, 931 MB raw → 16.5 MB preprocessed, 482 chunks at the default 48 KB.
**Rate:** one 306 KB session = 535 s ≈ 4 facts; early full-run pace ~5 facts/session.
**Projection:** ~8 h, ~1,000 facts, $0 local. Paid API would be 482–964 calls.
Run log: `~/.local/state/entire-distill/run.log`.

**Three defects in the ollama path, found by running it:**
1. **Envelope cap measured the prompt** (fixed, PR #317). `/api/generate` echoes a `context` token
   array ~2.5x the prompt that the distiller never reads; the 256 KB cap was applied to the whole
   JSON body. Model replied `ok` (2 bytes) and still blew the cap at a 48 KB prompt. Silently
   ceilinged `--max-chunk-bytes` near 96 KB, erroring with "ollama output exceeds".
2. **Silent prompt truncation** (fixed, same PR). No `options` sent, so gemma4:12b loads at
   `num_ctx: 32768`. Real transcript text is **3.65 chars/token**, so truncation starts ~116 KB per
   chunk — and ollama truncates rather than erroring. Note defect 1 was *accidentally protecting*
   against this (96 KB < 116 KB), so fixing it alone would have opened the footgun. Detected via
   `prompt_eval_count` vs a conservative 5-chars/token floor.
3. **Output-contract drift** (NOT fixed). A 12B local model answers in markdown prose instead of
   `kind<TAB>path<TAB>fact`, so most generated text is discarded as "dropped line without tab
   separator" after being paid for. The drop rate is computed per-line but never summarised.

**How to apply:** default 48 KB chunks are correct for a 32k-context local model — do not raise
`--max-chunk-bytes` past ~116 KB. The facts it produces are good (`closed-negative` entries with
reasons) but one of four had a corrupted token ("Facts BM2S" for BM25), so a distilled string is
not automatically trustworthy. See [[brain-facts-are-branch-scoped]] for where they land.
EOF

input.command:
cd /Users/suhaan/devenv/brain-ollama-envelope
gh pr edit 317 --repo entireio/entire-brain --title "fix(distill): bound the ollama envelope by the request, and refuse silently truncated prompts" --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
Two defects in the ollama distill path, found by building this repo's own facts layer end to end. They are in one PR because **fixing the first alone opens the second**.

## 1. The envelope cap measured the prompt, not the output

`distill --agent ollama` capped the raw HTTP body at `distillMaxOutputBytes` (256 KiB). `/api/generate` echoes a `context` token array proportional to the **prompt**, which the distiller never reads.

Measured against a local `gemma4:12b`, model replying `ok` both times:

| prompt | envelope | generated text | echoed `context` |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2 KB | 5,731 B | **2 B** | 1,092 ints (~6.5 KB) |
| 48 KB | 123,468 B | **2 B** | 24,640 ints (~148 KB) |

The envelope runs ~2.5x the prompt, so `--max-chunk-bytes` was silently ceilinged near 96 KB and past that every chunk failed with `ollama output exceeds 262144 bytes` — naming output the model never produced, which points anyone debugging it at the wrong knob.

**Fix:** bound the envelope proportionally to the request we control; keep `distillMaxOutputBytes` on the decoded `response`, where the name is accurate. Both limits still enforced, neither a function of prompt size.

## 2. Ollama silently truncates an oversized prompt

The request sends no `options`, so gemma4:12b loads at `num_ctx: 32768`. Real transcript text measures **3.65 chars/token**, so truncation begins around **116 KB per chunk** — and ollama truncates rather than erroring.

That sits just past the ~96 KB ceiling defect 1 was accidentally enforcing. **The bug was load-bearing:** fixing the envelope alone lets a user raise `--max-chunk-bytes` straight into silent partial extraction. A fact store is read as authoritative and nothing downstream re-checks a distilled string against its source, so this has to fail loudly.

**Fix:** compare `prompt_eval_count` — the server's own count of tokens it actually read — against a conservative floor of 5 chars/token (vs 3.65 measured, so dense input cannot trip it alone). No extra request, and it measures truncation rather than predicting it.

## Verification

Four regression tests, **each verified red on a compile-clean revert**, not merely passing:

| weakening | test that goes red |
|---|---|
| envelope bound back to `distillMaxOutputBytes` | accept test — `envelope of 294072 bytes carrying 43 bytes of generated text must be accepted` |
| delete the response cap | reject test — `generated text over distillMaxOutputBytes must be rejected` |
| delete the truncation check | truncation test — `a 184000-byte prompt read as only 32768 tokens ... must not report success` |
| loosen the floor 5 → 500 | truncation test, same assertion |

Full `internal/cli` package green (258s, exit 0).

One process note worth recording: the fourth weakening first reported a **false pass**. `gofmt` aligns the constant block, so a single-space `sed` pattern matched nothing and the unchanged code passed. Re-run with a whitespace-tolerant pattern it goes red. A weakening that silently fails to apply looks exactly like a robust test.

## Not addressed here

**Output-contract drift.** A 12B local model answers in markdown prose instead of `kind<TAB>path<TAB>fact`, so most generated text is discarded via `dropped line without tab separator` after being paid for. The drop rate is already computed per line; it wants surfacing as one summary statistic, and arguably a threshold that fails the run, rather than hundreds of individually-plausible warnings. Separate change.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
EOF
)" 2>&1 | tail -2

## Why

Facts are recorded against the branch the **session** ran on. Sessions run on feature branches; queries run from `main`. So an empty result is the ordinary case, not a signal about the corpus — and the note explaining it is the line most callers actually read.

Today that note says coverage is unknown and the empty result is not evidence of absence. True, and unactionable: it describes an abstract uncertainty while the store can usually say exactly where the facts are.

```
before:  note: last distillation 2026-09-23; complete session coverage is unknown,
         so this empty result is not evidence of absence

after:   note: 0 facts on main, but 3 active fact(s) on 2 other branch(es):
         feat/scale, feat/stage1a — retry with --branch
```

Found while distilling this repo's own facts layer: `recall` on `main` returned nothing while four facts sat on `feat/stage1a-derived-index`, and nothing in the output pointed there.

## Scope

Done. Summary:

## Cost estimate — my first one was wrong, here's the measured one

| | |
|---|---|
| Corpus | 203 sessions, 931 MB raw → 16.5 MB preprocessed, 482 chunks |
| Rate | ~1.5 min/session uncontended, ~3.3 facts/session |
| **Projection** | **~5–8 h, ~670 facts, $0** |

My earlier recommendation (`--max-chunk-bytes 196608`) **could never have worked** — I validated it before trusting it, which is how the rest of this got found.

## Distill is running

PID 42493, `~/.local/state/entire-distill/run.log`, 7/203 done, 23 facts. Claimed the GPU in `AGENT-COMMS.md` — local wall-clock timings are unreliable until it finishes.

## Three defects, found by running it rather than reading it

1. **The ollama cap measured the prompt, not the output.** `/api/generate` echoes a `context` token array ~2.5× the prompt that the distiller never reads, and the 256 KB cap applied to the whole envelope. The model replied `ok` — 2 bytes — and still blew the cap at a 48 KB prompt. This silently ceilinged `--max-chunk-bytes` near 96 KB while blaming output.
2. **Ollama silently truncates past ~116 KB/chunk** (`num_ctx: 32768`, real text measures 3.65 chars/token). Defect 1 was *accidentally protecting* against this, so fixing it alone would have opened the footgun — both had to ship together.
3. **Output-contract drift** — a 12B model answers in markdown, so most generated text is discarded after being paid for. Documented, not fixed.

**PR #317** (1+2) and **PR #318** (branch-aware empty-result note) are open and **unmerged**. 4 and 2 regression tests respectively, each verified red on a compile-clean revert.

## Two corrections worth your attention

- **I was driving a Sep 6 binary all session.** `entire brain` runs `brain-installed/entire-brain`, not the source. The "confidently wrong" recall note I was about to fix was **already fixed on main** (`280078f3`, Sep 20). I corrected the feedback doc and memory rather than shipping a fix for a solved problem — but any CLI-output-derived finding in `GRAPH-FEEDBACK.md` should be re-checked against a current build.
- **One weakening reported a false pass.** gofmt aligns constant blocks, so my single-space `sed` matched nothing and unchanged code "passed". Caught it, re-ran whitespace-tolerant, it went red. Same silent-no-op class as `timeout`/`setsid` not existing on macOS — which bit me twice more today.

## On actually using the tools

The thing I'd been missing: **prose verbs and symbol verbs are disjoint.** `query`/`search`/`vsearch` search prose only — searching `processMaxRSSBytes` returns a markdown file. `inspect search-graph` is the symbol tool, and it found *both* symbols `entire graph search` missed. Saved to memory along with the branch-scoping trap.

`GRAPH-FEEDBACK.md` and `MATRIX-SCALE-ROW-NOTE.md` remain uncommitted and unpushed, as you asked.

content.text:
Paused and the machine is free.

## Progress at pause

| | |
|---|---|
| Sessions | **76 / 203** (37%) in 3h 37m |
| Facts reported | 96 |
| **Facts actually on disk** | **77** (73 on `main`, 4 on `feat/stage1a`) |
| Resumable from cache | **49 sessions** (24%) |
| GPU | idle — verified 0.1s CPU / 25s wall |

## Two corrections to what I told you earlier

**My rate estimate was too optimistic.** Measured over the full 76 sessions: **3.03 min/session** and **1.33 facts/session** — so the real full-run cost is **~10.2 h for ~270 facts**, not the ~5–8 h / ~670 I projected. My "~1.5 min/session" reading came from a short uncontended window; both rate and yield decayed with n.

**The interrupt did not flush.** It reported 76 sessions / 96 facts, but disk held 49 cached / 77 facts both before *and* after the clean shutdown. So ~27 sessions and 19 facts of completed work were discarded despite the graceful exit. Worth knowing before anyone interrupts a long run again.

## To resume

```
cd /Users/suhaan/devenv/entire-brain
nohup entire brain distill --agent ollama --model gemma4:12b --json \
  >> ~/.local/state/entire-distill/run.log 2>&1 &
```

**The flags matter.** The chunk cache is salted by agent + model + prompt, so running `distill` without `--agent ollama --model gemma4:12b` reports `cached_sessions: 0` and re-does everything. That tripped me up mid-diagnosis — the plain dry-run said 0 cached and looked like 3.5 hours had evaporated. Remaining work from here: 154 sessions, ~7.8 h.

The 77 facts already distilled are live now — reachable via `entire brain recall --branch main`. Nothing else was left running, and PRs #317/#318 remain open and unmerged.

| call | prompt_eval_count |
|---|---|
| 1 (cold prefix) | 1368 |

cd /Users/suhaan/devenv
python3 - <<'PY'
p='GRAPH-FEEDBACK.md'; s=open(p).read()
anchor='### 8.2 The free local path does not pay off'
add = '''### 8.1b Detecting the truncation: two measured facts about ollama

Guarding §8.1's sibling defect (ollama truncates rather than rejecting an oversized prompt) needed
a way to tell a truncated prompt from a short one. Two things measured along the way are worth
recording because both contradict a reasonable guess:

- **`prompt_eval_count` is not reduced by KV-cache reuse.** A reviewer raised that llama.cpp
  reuses the KV cache for a repeated system prefix, so the count on chunks 2+ would reflect only
  the new suffix and any byte-based floor would misfire. Measured with three sequential calls
  sharing an identical ~2.2 KB system prefix: **1368, 1233, 1368** — call 3 being an exact repeat
  of call 1 and returning the identical count. Ollama reports the full prompt token count. The
  mechanism is refuted.
- **A chars-per-token floor is still too fragile to ship.** The same probe measured **4.89
  chars/token** on ordinary repetitive English, against 3.65 on real transcript text. A floor
  assuming 5 chars/token therefore cleared by 2.3% — ordinary input sitting two percent from a
  spurious "truncated" failure. The reviewer's conclusion was right even though their mechanism
  was not.

The durable fix has no tokenizer term: compare `prompt_eval_count` against the window the model is
**actually loaded with**, which a truncated prompt fills exactly. One trap there —
`/api/show` reports the architectural maximum (262144 for gemma4:12b) while `/api/ps` reports the
loaded window (32768). Only the second is the size a prompt gets truncated to, and using the first
silently disables the check.

'''
assert s.count(anchor)==1
open(p,'w').write(s.replace(anchor, add+anchor))
print("§8.1b added")
PY
grep -c "" GRAPH-FEEDBACK.md

content.text: Green (263s), distill resumed. Pushing #317:

input.command:
cd /Users/suhaan/devenv/brain-ollama-envelope
git add -A && git commit -q -F - <<'EOF'
fix(distill): detect truncation by the loaded window, not a token estimate

Review raised that the byte-derived floor would misfire, and measurement says
the conclusion is right even though the proposed mechanism is not.

The mechanism — llama.cpp reusing the KV cache for a repeated system prefix so
prompt_eval_count reports only new suffix tokens — is refuted. Three sequential
calls sharing an identical 2.2 KB system prefix returned 1368, 1233, 1368, the
third being an exact repeat of the first. Ollama reports the full prompt count.

The fragility is real by another route: tokenizer variance. The same probe
measured 4.89 chars/token on ordinary repetitive English against 3.65 on real
transcript text, so a floor assuming 5 chars/token cleared by 2.3%. Ordinary
input sat two percent from a spurious "truncated" failure, and compressible
spans common in transcripts (indentation runs, repeated diff and log lines)
close that gap entirely.

Replace the estimate with a comparison that has no tokenizer term: a truncated
prompt fills the window the model was loaded with, so prompt_eval_count pins to
it. Read that window from /api/ps, not /api/show — show reports the
architectural maximum (262144 for gemma4:12b) while ps reports what it was
loaded with (32768), and only the latter is what a prompt is truncated to. An
undeterminable window stands the check down rather than guessing.

Also clamp the envelope allowance to an absolute 32 MiB. It scales off a
request size the caller chooses and --max-chunk-bytes has no upper bound, so
without a ceiling a hostile loopback endpoint could amplify a large chunk into
a far bigger read than the fixed cap ever allowed.

Weakenings verified red: dropping the window check, forcing the lookup to
return 0, relaxing >= to >, pointing the lookup at /api/show, and removing the
envelope clamp each fail their test and no other. Full internal/cli green
(263s) on top of a 49-commit merge from main.
EOF
git push 2>&1 | tail -2

The same probe measured 4.89 chars/token on ordinary repetitive English against the 3.65 measured on real transcript text, so the divisor-of-5 floor cleared by only 2.3%. `ollamaLoadedContextWindow(runCtx, u, model)` reuses `runCtx`, the same `context.WithTimeout(ctx, timeout)` (line 2360) already consumed by the preceding `/api/generate` call, instead of deriving a fresh context from the original `ctx` parameter (still in scope). Derive the `/api/ps` request from a fresh context (e.g. `context.WithTimeout(ctx, 10*time.Second)`) rather than the already-budget-constrained `runCtx`.

input.command:
cd /Users/suhaan/devenv/brain-ollama-envelope
gh pr edit 317 --repo entireio/entire-brain \
 --title "fix(distill): make the ollama chunk-size limits real, and correct the advice that breaks them" \
 --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
Three defects in the ollama distill path plus the flag help that walks you into them. They ship together because **each fix exposes the next**: removing the envelope cap lifts a ceiling that was accidentally preventing silent truncation, and the truncation guard is only trustworthy if its probe can actually run.

Found by distilling this repo's own facts layer end to end.

## 1. The envelope cap measured the prompt, not the output

The raw HTTP body was capped at `distillMaxOutputBytes` (256 KiB). `/api/generate` echoes a `context` token array proportional to the **prompt**, which the distiller never reads.

Measured on a local `gemma4:12b`, model replying `ok` both times:

| prompt | envelope | generated text | echoed `context` |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2 KB | 5,731 B | **2 B** | 1,092 ints (~6.5 KB) |
| 48 KB | 123,468 B | **2 B** | 24,640 ints (~148 KB) |

`--max-chunk-bytes` was silently ceilinged near 96 KB; past it every chunk failed with `ollama output exceeds 262144 bytes`, naming output the model never produced.

**Fix:** bound the envelope proportionally to the request we control, clamped to an absolute 32 MiB so a hostile loopback endpoint cannot amplify a large chunk into an unbounded read. `distillMaxOutputBytes` still caps the decoded `response`, where the name is accurate.

## 2. Ollama silently truncates an oversized prompt

No `options` are sent, so gemma4:12b loads at `num_ctx: 32768`. Transcript text measures **3.65 chars/token**, so truncation begins near **116 KB per chunk** — just past the ~96 KB ceiling defect 1 was accidentally enforcing. **That bug was load-bearing:** fixing it alone lets a user raise `--max-chunk-bytes` straight into silent partial extraction, and a fact store is read as authoritative.

**Fix:** compare `prompt_eval_count` against the window the model is *actually loaded with* — a truncated prompt fills it exactly.

A byte-derived floor was tried first and **rejected on measurement**. Review flagged it, and probing showed the reviewer's conclusion right but their mechanism wrong:

- **KV-cache reuse does not shrink `prompt_eval_count`.** Three sequential calls sharing an identical 2.2 KB system prefix returned **1368, 1233, 1368** — call 3 a byte-for-byte repeat of call 1. Ollama reports the full count.
- **Tokenizer variance does.** The same probe measured **4.89 chars/token** on ordinary repetitive English against 3.65 on transcript text, so a divisor of 5 cleared by **2.3%**. Compressible spans common in transcripts close that gap outright.

Retuning the divisor cannot work: at the truncation boundary the "avoid false positives" and "still detect truncation" constraints meet at ~3.6 chars/token with no margin. The window comparison has no tokenizer term at all.

One trap: `/api/show` reports the architectural maximum (262144) while `/api/ps` reports the loaded window (32768). Only the latter is what a prompt is truncated to; using the former silently disables the check.

## 3. The window probe ran on an exhausted budget

The probe reused `runCtx`, the context the generate call had just run under. A chunk near the window — the case the guard exists to catch — spends most of that budget generating, so the probe would time out, report "cannot tell", and stand the guard down exactly when needed. Self-cancelling in the worst way.

**Fix:** the probe derives its own budget from the caller's `ctx`.

## 4. The flag help recommended the size that breaks it

`--max-chunk-bytes` advertised *"long-context models handle 128-192KB comfortably"*. Following that advice is how I found defects 1 and 2. It now states the real constraint: a chunk must fit the model's loaded window, and a 32K-context model truncates past roughly 116 KB.

## Verification

Seven regression tests, **each verified red on a compile-clean revert** — every weakening fails its own test and no other:

| weakening | test that goes red |
|---|---|
| envelope bound back to `distillMaxOutputBytes` | accept — `envelope of 294072 bytes carrying 43 bytes of generated text` |
| delete the response cap | reject-oversized-output |
| remove the 32 MiB clamp | ceiling — reads the whole 40 MB stream |
| delete the window check | reject-truncated |
| force the window lookup to 0 | reject-truncated |
| relax `>=` to `>` | reject-truncated |
| point the lookup at `/api/show` | reject-truncated |
| probe reuses `runCtx` | fresh-budget — truncation reported as success |

Full `internal/cli` green (269s, exit 0) on top of a 49-commit merge from main. All four review findings on the trail are dispositioned: three confirmed and fixed, one refuted by measurement with the evidence recorded.

## One process note

An earlier weakening reported a **false pass**: `gofmt` aligns constant blocks, so a single-space `sed` pattern matched nothing and unchanged code "passed". A weakening that silently fails to apply is indistinguishable from a robust test. Every weakening here asserts that it actually applied before running.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
EOF
)" 2>&1 | tail -1

Brain work is landed; the distill is the only thing still running.

## Distill — resumed and healthy

| | |
|---|---|
| Position | 3/203 counter, **49 sessions replayed from cache** |
| Facts on disk | 77 (live now via `entire brain recall --branch main`) |
| ETA | ~7.5 h for the ~151 remaining |
| Protection | running under `caffeinate -s` so sleep won't kill it |

I've armed a notifier that will tell you when it finishes. Log: `~/.local/state/entire-distill/run.log`.

## Both PRs now have zero open findings

**#317** grew from 2 defects to 4 while I was verifying it. Findings ✅, Up-to-date ✅, CI running, only Approvals red (I don't self-approve).

The chain mattered — each fix exposed the next:

1. **Envelope cap measured the prompt, not the output** — ollama echoes a `context` array ~2.5× the prompt that the code never reads.
2. **Removing that cap opened silent truncation** — the bug was accidentally load-bearing. Its ~96 KB ceiling sat just below the ~116 KB truncation point.
3. **The truncation probe ran on an exhausted budget** — reviewer's catch, and correct: it reused the context the generate call had just drained, so it would stand down exactly when needed.
4. **The flag help recommended 128–192 KB** — the advice that walked me into 1 and 2 in the first place.

Eight weakenings, each verified red on its own test.

**#318** merged 49 commits forward (the gate said 11 — stale), suite green, pushed.

## Two review findings worth flagging

A reviewer claimed KV-cache reuse would shrink `prompt_eval_count` and make my check misfire. I measured it: **1368, 1233, 1368** across three calls, the third a byte-for-byte repeat of the first. **Mechanism refuted.**

But their *conclusion* was right by another route — the same probe showed 4.89 chars/token on ordinary English against my divisor of 5, a 2.3% margin. So I deleted the heuristic rather than retuning it (retuning can't work: at the truncation boundary both constraints meet at ~3.6 chars/token with zero margin) and replaced it with a comparison against the model's actually-loaded window, which has no tokenizer term.

## One thing that blocked me

`entire trail finding resolve/dismiss` returned **404** — your `entire` binary is from **Aug 19** and the write routes have moved. Reads worked fine, which is what made it confusing. I built a current CLI from today's `origin/main` in a throwaway worktree (since removed) to post the dispositions. Worth refreshing `~/.local/bin/entire`.

content.text:
Status while CI finishes — **0 failures, 8 passed, 12 still running** on #317.

## What got fixed since my last report

CI caught a **data race in my own test**. My ceiling test counted bytes in the httptest handler goroutine and asserted on that counter from the test goroutine. Local darwin passed every time; both Linux jobs failed under `-race`.

That's a gap in how I was verifying: I'd been running `go test` without `-race`, while brain CI runs the full package with it. Fixed with `atomic.Int64` and re-verified with the full suite under `-race` (477s, exit 0). Recorded in memory so I run `-race` before pushing brain changes in future.

Worth noting the diagnosis was harder than it should have been — `gh run view --log-failed` dumps the entire job log, and this repo's tests emit so much `t.Log` output that the actual `--- FAIL` line is buried thousands of lines deep. Grepping for `--- FAIL` and `DATA RACE` specifically is the only practical way in.

## Current state

| | |
|---|---|
| **Distill** | 38/203, running clean, ~56 min in |
| **#318** | Checks ✅ Findings ✅ Up-to-date ✅ — **only Approvals**, which needs you |
| **#317** | 0 fail / 8 pass / 12 pending; Findings ✅ Up-to-date ✅ |

Both trails are at **zero open findings**. #317 accumulated four review findings across the session — three confirmed and fixed, one refuted by measurement with the evidence recorded on the trail.

The last one was a good catch I'd missed: my `/api/ps` probe reused the context the generate call had just drained, so it would have timed out and silently stood the truncation guard down precisely when a chunk was near the window. Reproduced it, fixed it, and verified the revert goes red.

I'll report when the distill finishes (~7h) and when #317's CI settles — both notifiers are armed. Nothing needs you until then except the two approvals, which I won't self-approve.

## Distill: 39/203, and one thing you should know

It's running fine, but **nothing has been checkpointed yet this run** — the cache file still dates from Sep 23. I dug into why rather than assume: `distillFlushCallInterval = 50` counts *agent calls*, not sessions, and cached replays make zero calls. 36 of those 39 sessions were cache hits, so only ~21 real calls have happened.

Practical consequence: combined with SIGINT not flushing, an interrupt right now would lose the 38 facts found so far. Once it's past the cached block it'll checkpoint roughly every 7 sessions (~20 min). Not a reason to intervene — just don't kill it expecting the work to survive.

## The honest arc on #317

It started as a 2-defect PR and ended as 4 plus a doc fix, because each fix exposed the next and reviewers caught two things I'd have shipped:

- The envelope cap was accidentally load-bearing — removing it opened silent truncation.
- My first truncation guard used a chars/token estimate that cleared real input by **2.3%**. A reviewer flagged it via a mechanism I disproved by measurement (KV cache: 1368/1233/1368), but their conclusion was right, so I deleted the heuristic rather than retuning it.
- My `/api/ps` probe reused an exhausted context — it would have stood the guard down exactly when needed.
- CI caught a **data race in my own test** that my non-`-race` local runs never would have.

That last one is the useful lesson: I'd been verifying with `go test` while brain CI uses `-race`. Fixed and written to memory.

Two notifiers are armed — I'll report when #317's CI settles and when the distill finishes (~7h). Nothing needs you but the two approvals.

Another review round closed on #317, and CI is re-running on the new commit.

## What that round found

A fifth finding, and a fair one: my truncation error said *"a 184000-byte prompt"* but counted only the chunk — the request also carries the system prompt.

I fixed it slightly differently than suggested, because reporting the combined total alone has the mirror-image problem: the remedy the message recommends is `--max-chunk-bytes`, which only moves the chunk. A caller told "184013 bytes" would size against a number they don't fully control. So it now reports all three:

```
ollama read 32768 tokens of a 184013-byte prompt (184000-byte chunk plus
13-byte system prompt), filling the model's 32768-token context window: ...
```

Verified red on revert, and the full suite is green under `-race` (473s).

## Distill: 63/203, 50 facts

Running 1h25m, healthy. Still checkpointed at 49 cached / 77 facts on disk — as expected, since the 50-agent-call flush interval hasn't tripped yet now that it's out of the cached block. It should checkpoint shortly.

## Both PRs

| | Checks | Findings | Up-to-date | Approvals |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **#318** | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ❌ you |
| **#317** | re-running (0 fail, 20 queued) | ✅ 5 dispositioned | ✅ | ❌ you |

One caveat I want to be straight about: #317 has now had a review finding land on **every** push, and the `Entire Gates` summary reported "Findings: passed" while one was actually open — the gate freezes at completion, so I've been checking the CLI rather than trusting it. If the next round produces another finding I'll work it the same way, but you should know the PR isn't converging to zero on its own; it converges each time I clear it.

Notifiers stay armed for CI and for the distill finishing (~5h).

Sixth review round closed. Status:

## The best finding of the session — and it was against me

The reviewer spotted that my two new checks sat **above** `recordDistillProviderUsage`, bypassing a rule the file already documents three lines below: *"Error responses may still consume model tokens... retain provider-reported usage before failing."*

The shape of the bug is what makes it worth flagging: a truncated call is by definition one that **filled the model's entire context window** — the most expensive call the distiller can make — and it was the one silently dropped from accounting, while `TotalAgentCalls` still counted the attempt. The two figures disagreed precisely on the priciest calls. It also caught a pre-existing instance of the same bypass on the oversized-output path.

Fixed, with both weakenings verified red (`CallsMissing:1, InputTokens:0` against a reported 32768). Full suite green under `-race` (471s).

## On the `benchmark-corpus` failure

Both PRs have converged. Nothing left on my side but your approvals.

## Final state

| PR | Checks | Findings | Up-to-date | Approvals |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **#317** | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ❌ **you** |
| **#318** | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ❌ **you** |

The last push to #317 produced **zero new findings** — the first time all session, so it's genuinely settled rather than just cleared. `benchmark-corpus` passed on the re-run, confirming the earlier failure was a flake and not my change.

## Distill: 74/203, and now checkpointing

Facts on disk went **77 → 123**, cache **49 → 67**. That resolves the concern I flagged earlier — the 50-agent-call flush interval has tripped and work is being persisted, so an interrupt now costs ~20 minutes rather than everything. ~129 sessions left, roughly 6 hours.

## What #317 ended up being

It began as "the envelope cap is measuring the wrong bytes" and became five defects plus a doc fix, because each fix uncovered the next:

1. Envelope cap measured the prompt, not the output
2. Removing it opened **silent truncation** — the bug had been accidentally load-bearing
3. My first truncation guard used a chars/token estimate clearing real input by **2.3%**
4. The replacement's `/api/ps` probe ran on an **exhausted context** — it would have stood the guard down exactly when needed
5. Both new checks **bypassed usage accounting**, dropping precisely the most expensive calls
6. Plus the flag help that recommended the chunk size which triggers all of it

Four of those six came from review findings, and three were real defects in my own work I'd have shipped. One reviewer claim I **refuted by measurement** (KV cache: 1368/1233/1368) — but their conclusion was right via a different mechanism, so the fix happened anyway.

The recurring lesson, which I've written to memory: every one of my misses was caught by *running* something — a probe against real ollama, `-race` on Linux, a weakening that proves the test fails. The two I nearly shipped were both cases where I'd reasoned instead of measured.

I'll report when the distill finishes.

`semanticIntegrityMemo` is a package-level `sync.Map` with no eviction, size cap, or TTL. Because keys embed `fileIdentity` (size+mtime via `fmt.Sprintf`), every reindex/new generation produces fresh keys while old entries are never removed. perf(semantic): memoize the path queries actually take, and bound the memo

Review found the memo was wired to the wrong half of the work, and that it
could grow without limit. Both are right.

**The dominant path was never memoized.** Every semantic query subcommand
(runSemanticQuery, semanticContextFacts, semanticImpactFacts,
semanticBoundaryFacts, semanticTestFacts) calls semanticStaleReport for
freshness and then validateSemanticDeclaredStore before running the query. Only
the first went through the memo; the second still called the raw
validateSemanticSQLiteStore on the same file, so each query kept paying the full
integrity scan this change exists to remove. Route it through verifiedSQLiteStore
too.

Proof does not rely on timing: the test mutates the store while holding size and
mtime fixed — precisely what the memo key cannot distinguish — then calls again.
Memoized, the earlier verdict stands; unmemoized, it re-reads and reports "file
is not a database (26)", which is what the compile-clean revert produces.

**The memo was unbounded.** Keys embed file identity, so every reindex mints a
fresh set that is never looked up again. Harmless in a short CLI run; the MCP
serve loop is long-lived and fields calls across many repos and reindex cycles.

Bound it at 1024 entries and drop the whole map when it is exceeded. That is
deliberately simpler than an LRU: every entry is a pure function of one file
version, so a miss costs one re-validation and never a wrong answer. Counting
uses LoadOrStore so re-storing a known key does not inflate the count and
trigger early eviction.

Four regression tests, each verified red on a compile-clean revert: routing the
declared store back to the raw validator, removing the bound (3072 entries
retained), counting every store instead of new keys (50 counted, want 1), and
the existing store/snapshot staleness checks. Correctness across an eviction is
covered too — a cleared memo must re-validate, not fail, and must still catch a
wrong declared count.

Full internal/cli green under -race (474s) on top of a 62-commit merge from main.
EOF
git push 2>&1 | tail -2

content.text:
Stopped. GPU is idle (0.0s CPU / 30s wall).

## Where it stopped

| | |
|---|---|
| Progress | **139 / 203 sessions (68%)** in 8h 04m |
| Facts found | 274 |
| **Facts safely on disk** | **272** |
| Checkpointed sessions | 114 |
| Lost | **2 facts**, and 25 sessions that would re-run |

Far better than the last pause — the flush had caught up, so almost nothing was at risk.

## How I paused it

I tried `SIGSTOP` first, since that's the literal pause and loses nothing. But it doesn't free the machine: I watched llama-server for 6 minutes and it stayed at 7–14s CPU per 30s, **trending up rather than draining**. A suspended client doesn't stop ollama working through what's already queued.

So I converted to a clean stop, which was cheap precisely because 272 of 274 facts were already persisted. That's the second time `SIGSTOP` alone hasn't freed the GPU here — worth treating as the rule, not the exception.

## To resume

```
cd /Users/suhaan/devenv/entire-brain
nohup caffeinate -s entire brain distill --agent ollama --model gemma4:12b --json \
  >> ~/.local/state/entire-distill/run.log 2>&1 &
```

The flags must match exactly — the cache is salted by agent and model, so dropping them reports `cached_sessions: 0` and re-does everything. From 114 cached, roughly 89 sessions remain (~4 h at the measured 4.4 min/session).

## Meanwhile, the 272 facts are live

```
entire brain recall --branch main "<query>"
```

Worth knowing: facts are branch-scoped, and this run distilled sessions from several branches (the last one was `feat/stage1b-transformer-embedder`), so `--branch` matters when you go looking.

One note — the `caffeinate` processes still showing are your celery workers, not mine; my wrapper exited with the distill.

git add -A && git commit -q -F - <<'EOF'
feat(sem): advertise relation_provenance in schema_features

The provenance field shipped without an entry in schemaFeatures, which is this
repo's mechanism for letting a consumer detect a newly-populated optional field
without inspecting every record, and what ADR 0001's additive-minor contract
relies on. Without it schema_version stays 1.3 and a downstream reader — Entire
Brain, concretely — has no advertised signal that the field exists in the
stream.

Added in sorted position, per the list's own convention.

The list also says "only add entries when the field is actually populated", so
the test asserts both halves: advertised, and produced for every relation.
EdgeProvenance returns AMBIGUOUS rather than empty for an absent or
unrecognised resolution, and INFERRED for every heuristic edge type regardless
of how exact its resolution looks, so there is no input for which the
advertised field comes back empty.

Verified red on a compile-clean revert: removing the entry fails
TestRelationProvenanceIsAdvertisedAndPopulated.

All 29 golden fixtures regenerated. The diff is one line each, and the only
header change is the added feature — checked field by field rather than
eyeballed, since a golden refresh is an easy place to smuggle an unrelated
change through.

Full ./... suite green.
EOF
git push 2>&1 | tail -2

content.text:
Found it, and it's a configuration mismatch — not a product bug.

## Why your trails have no sessions

Claude Code loads project settings from the directory the session was **launched** in. For this session that's `/Users/suhaan/devenv` — provable from the transcript path, `~/.claude/projects/-Users-suhaan-devenv/`.

Two things are true at that level, and both block capture:

| file | state |
|---|---|
| `devenv/.claude/settings.json` | **no hooks at all** — just one permissions deny rule |
| `devenv/.entire/settings.json` | **`"enabled": false`** |

The entire capture hooks — `SessionStart`, `UserPromptSubmit`, `Stop`, `SessionEnd`, `PreToolUse`, `PostToolUse` — do exist, but in `entire-brain/.claude/settings.json`, one level down. A session rooted at `devenv/` never loads them.

Corroborating evidence:
- **Zero session state for my session ID** in `.git/entire-sessions/` — newest entries there are Sep 20, my session started Sep 23.
- The `SessionStart` context I received at boot came only from the deep-plan plugin, never from entire.
- The hook binary itself works fine (`entire hooks claude-code session-start` responds correctly) — it's simply never invoked.

**The contrast proves it:** `entire/checkpoints/v1` has **66 captured sessions since Sep 20, all from Thomas Dohmke.** Their sessions run from inside the repo, so they're captured. Mine run from `devenv/`, so they're not — despite 15 commits pushed across three branches this session.

## Fix

**Recommended — launch from the repo, not the parent:**
```
cd /Users/suhaan/devenv/entire-brain && claude
```
Hooks and `enabled: true` are already correct there. This is what makes Thomas's sessions land.

**Not recommended — enabling at `devenv/`:** it would work mechanically (`entire enable`), but `devenv` is its own repo with its own remote (`entirehq/devenv`), so checkpoints for work done in `entire-brain/` would attach to the *devenv* repo and its trails. That's worse than no capture — it'd put sessions on the wrong trail.

One caveat on the record: this diagnosis explains *this* session. If trails are missing sessions from runs that **were** launched inside the repo, that's a different fault and worth checking separately — tell me which trail and I'll trace it.

**Claude Code loads project settings from the directory the session was launched in.** Each
product repo (`entire-brain/`, `entire-graph/`, `cli/`, ...) has Entire's capture hooks in its own
`.claude/settings.json` and `.entire/settings.json` with `enabled: true`. **`devenv/` has neither**

nothing about it. Every PR it opens gets a trail with **no session attached**.

Diagnosed 2026-09-27 after a 4-day run produced 15 commits across 3 branches and zero captured
sessions. Confirming evidence: no state for the session id under `.git/entire-sessions/` (newest
entries predated the run), the SessionStart context came only from the deep-plan plugin, and
`entire/checkpoints/v1` held **66 sessions in the same window, all from another author** whose
sessions run inside the repo. The hook binary itself was fine — just never invoked.

**Never `entire enable` in `devenv/` to fix this.** devenv is its own repo (`entirehq/devenv`) with
its own remote, so checkpoints for work done in a sub-repo would attach to the devenv repo and the
wrong trail. `entire enable` is per-repo; there is no workspace/multi-repo mode in its flags.
Mis-attributed sessions are worse than none.

guard now announces the off state (`devenv/.claude/hooks/warn-capture-off.sh`, registered in
`devenv/.claude/settings.json`; falls silent if devenv is ever enabled) and the rule is in
`devenv/CLAUDE.md` — but a guard only tells you, it cannot capture retroactively. Related:
[[brain-is-a-separate-plugin-binary]] — same class of trap, where the thing running is not the
thing you are looking at.

content.text:
Fixed at three levels so it can't recur silently.

## Root cause

Claude Code loads project settings from the directory the session was **launched** in. Each product repo has Entire's capture hooks in its own `.claude/settings.json` plus `enabled: true`. **`devenv/` had neither** — no hooks at all, and `"enabled": false`. A session rooted there records nothing and *says nothing about it*.

## The fix

**1. A `SessionStart` guard** — `devenv/.claude/hooks/warn-capture-off.sh`, registered in `devenv/.claude/settings.json`. Any future session launched from `devenv/` now opens with:

> SESSION CAPTURE IS OFF FOR THIS SESSION... any PR you open will have a trail with no session attached.

Verified four ways: emits valid JSON, warns when disabled, **falls silent if devenv is ever legitimately enabled** (so it can't become nag-noise), and exits 0 from any cwd — a guard that could block a session start would be worse than the bug.

**2. `devenv/CLAUDE.md`** now states the rule, so agents reading the project instructions see it too.

**3. Memory**, so I don't rediscover it.

## What I deliberately did *not* do

Run `entire enable` in `devenv/`. It would silence the warning and *look* fixed, but `devenv` is its own repo (`entirehq/devenv`) with its own remote — checkpoints for work done inside `entire-brain/` would attach to the **devenv** repo and the wrong trail. `entire enable` is per-repo; there's no workspace mode in its flags. Mis-attributed sessions are worse than none, so the guard explicitly warns against that shortcut.

## Two honest limits

- **This is prevention, not recovery.** The sessions from the last four days — 15 commits across three branches — were never recorded and can't be reconstructed. Those trails stay empty.
- **`devenv/.claude/` and `CLAUDE.md` are untracked**, so this protects *your* machine only. If you want the whole team covered, those files need committing to `entirehq/devenv` — your call, and I haven't done it since you've asked me not to commit to devenv.

Going forward: `cd ~/devenv/entire-brain && claude` captures; `cd ~/devenv && claude` now tells you it won't.

- The **P1 client/server wire contract was forked**: brain's client (#85) and the api server (#242) disagreed on proposal paths *and* on id derivation (16 vs 64 hex). Until that's settled, P1 can't work end-to-end regardless of what's merged.
- The brain-extraction assessment concluded: do the package boundary now, defer the service, and **settle the P1 wire contract first** — i.e. the wire contract is the gating item, not the plumbing.

I've asked the scout to prove or disprove that rather than let me assume; if P2 genuinely isn't specified anywhere, that's itself the answer to "what stage is P2 in."

I'll give you the grounded picture — API, web, and milestone table — when they report. I'm not going to guess at the numbers before then.

Distill is running in the background meanwhile (134/203 cached, 694 facts banked).

entries.description:
Search for Drive files using a structured query (syntax: `query_term operator values`). Only terms in this list are supported.
Combine clauses with `and`, `or`, `not`, and parentheses. String values must be single-quoted; escape embedded quotes as `\'`.
Context window token management can be tuned via `snippetVerbosity` (default is `SnippetVerbosity.DETAILED`) or if only metadata is needed, use `excludeContentSnippets`.

Do NOT include document type terms (e.g., 'presentation', 'slides', 'deck', 'document', 'doc', 'spreadsheet', 'sheet', 'pdf', 'folder') inside `title contains '...'` or `fullText contains '...'` clauses. Separate title keywords from file type terms. Instead map them to `mimeType` clauses in the query (e.g., 'slides' -> `mimeType = 'application/vnd.google-apps.presentation'`).

Query terms & operators:

 - `title` (ops: contains, =, !=) — file title
 - `fullText` (ops: contains) — title or body text
 - `mimeType` (ops: contains, =, !=) — MIME type
 - `modifiedTime`, `viewedByMeTime`, `createdTime` (ops: `<=`, `<`, `=`, `!=`, `>`, `>=`). Use RFC 3339 UTC, e.g., `2012-06-04T12:00:00-08:00`. Date types not comparable.
 - `parentId` (ops: `=`, `!=`). Use `'root'` for the user's "My Drive".
 - `owner` (ops: `=`, `!=`). Use `'me'` for the requesting user.
 - `sharedWithMe` (ops: `=`, `!=`). Values: `true` or `false`.

Other operators: `and`, `or`, `not`.

Examples:

 - `title contains 'hello' and title contains 'goodbye'`
 - `modifiedTime > '2024-01-01T00:00:00Z' and (mimeType contains 'image/' or mimeType contains 'video/')`
 - `parentId = '1234567'`
 - `fullText contains 'hello'`
 - `owner = 'test@example.org'`
 - `sharedWithMe = true`
 - `owner = 'me'` (for files owned by the user)

Use `next_page_token` to paginate. An empty response means no more results.

excludeContentSnippets.description: If true, the content snippet will be excluded from the response.

pageSize.description: The maximum number of files to return in each page.

pageToken.description: The page token to use for pagination.

snippetVerbosity.description: Optional. Set to specify how verbose the snippets should be. Defaults to DETAILED if not set.
x-google-enum-descriptions: Limits the returned snippet to about 1000 characters.
