input.plan:
# Brain + Graph v1 readiness

## Context

Three streams of evidence converged this week:

1. **A user install report (Joseph)** — distill stalled at 75/237; `AGENTS.md`/`CLAUDE.md` never
   appeared at repo level; doc ambiguity about where to run setup.
2. **Seven issues filed 2026-10-02** by two external testers (leine4550, peyton-alt).
3. **Two full agent transcripts** (Claude Code and Codex, same prompts, same repo) showing agents
   not using Brain or Graph.

Investigation of all three found that the headline problem is **not** that agents are habitual.
Three distinct, verified causes sit underneath it, and all are fixable.

**Already fixed and merged:** #316 (semantic memo on the wrong path, unbounded, unlinearized),
#317 (ollama envelope cap measuring the prompt, silent truncation, probe on an exhausted budget,
usage-accounting bypass, misleading flag help). **Open and green:** #306, #318, #320, #321.

This plan covers what is *not* taken care of.

---

## The three root causes

### 1. Brain's guide instructs agents to skip the tools

`internal/agentsetup/files.go:1-3` claims the package is "mirrored byte-for-byte in both
repositories". It is not. entire-graph carries directive text; entire-brain still carries a
permissive regression from 2026-09-14.

| entire-graph `guide.go:78-81` | entire-brain `guide.go:8-9`, `:31`, `:68` |
|---|---|
| "Your FIRST action … **MUST** be ONE Graph query" | "**Directly inspect source** when the task already provides sufficient locations" |
| "Do not skip the query on the grounds that the available context feels sufficient" | "**Skip ceremonial queries** for small edits and follow-up work" |
| | "Useful locations from the brief do not require a redundant Graph query" |

Claude's own transcript: *"The agent guide says to start substantive tasks with `entire brain
brief` and use Graph for code discovery. I skipped that."* It was following the guide it was given.

**`internal/agentsetup/coordination_test.go:137` and `scripts/test-agent-coordination.py:69`
actively ban the strings `"FIRST action"` and `"SEARCH FIRST"`** — and the same test *requires*
`"sufficient locations"` to be present. The permissive wording is enforced by CI in both
directions. Verified directly, not taken from a report.

**Graph has already diagnosed and fixed this.** Its `coordination_test.go:142-145` says:

> *"'FIRST action' and 'SEARCH FIRST' used to be banned here alongside those probes. They are not
> probes; they are the directive that makes the product get used, and **banning them was benchmark
> arm-fairness doctrine applied to shipped text.**"*

That is the root cause, and it is a good mistake: arm-fairness is correct for benchmarks — you
cannot give one arm instructions the other lacks — and was then applied to the guide that ships to
users, where there is no other arm. Graph's `guide.go:8` now reads "TWO KINDS OF WORDING LIVE IN
THIS PACKAGE, AND THEY MUST NOT BE UNIFIED", and it added `TestNormalGuideStaysDirective`.

So PR 3 is not reversing a deliberate product decision. It is **porting a fix graph already made
and documented**, for a cause graph already named. Brain never caught up.

Graph's guide (`guide.go:9-27`) states the measured cost: *"332 graph calls against 96,987
exploration calls (0.34%), and the graph-first rate was 0 in every session sampled."*

### 2. The tools punish the agent that does comply

From the Claude transcript, when finally instructed to run them:

| tool | result |
|---|---|
| `brain_status` | Error: 124,295 chars — exceeds maximum allowed tokens |
| `brain_brief` | Error: 125,822 chars — exceeds maximum allowed tokens |
| `brain_impact` | Error: 61,580 chars — exceeds maximum allowed tokens |
| `brain_entity_history` | `"matches": []` |
| `brain_regressions` | `"no code identifiers found"`, `scanned_files: 0` |

A context-saving tool that overflows context is worse than no tool. `mcp_response_budget.go:54`
exists but is only a byte-budget *notice*.

### 3. Warnings and failures are silently dropped

A sweep found four HIGH instances of the class that has already cost this project repeatedly.
Worst: `internal/cli/semantic.go:2380` — `FilterWarnings` drops any warning whose Detail merely
*contains* a `.brainignore` pattern, by substring with no path parse. This repo's `.brainignore`
line 1 is `entire-brain`, a substring of every absolute path in it, so **every index warning is
discarded** and status reports a clean index that silently missed files.

### Also confirmed

- **Codex could not use Brain at all** — `entire` does not expose `brain`; it found the local
  executable by accident. Packaging/discovery gap, separate from compliance.
- **entire-graph ships no MCP server.** In an MCP-first harness the "MUST run a Graph query"
  instruction names a tool the agent does not have. 37 `brain_*` tools exist; **zero** tool
  descriptions mention grep, "first", "instead of" or "before".
- **`hook pre-edit` already exists** (`internal/cli/hook_cmd.go`, shipped in merged PR #24) and
  **nothing wires it**. Not in any settings template, not emitted by `init-agents`.
- The nested `entire-brain/` clone degrades Graph's index:
  `W_GIT_WORKTREE_FALLBACK: nested .git marker at "entire-brain/.git"`.

---

## Decisions, and why

**Three stacked PRs, not one.** PR1 and PR2 both touch `semantic.go` and `distill_cmd.go`, so they
genuinely conflict — stacking is correct here rather than cosmetic. Risk to accept: a stall in PR1
blocks 2 and 3. Mitigation: PR1 is the smallest and most obviously correct.

**Guide text before enforcement hook.** The guide currently says the opposite of what we want;
changing text is free and addresses the cause. The hook is belt-and-braces and goes in the same
PR, but we measure the guide change on its own first so we learn which one worked.

**Port graph's fix rather than invent one.** I was ready to flag the directive-wording ban as
needing the author's sign-off. Checking graph first showed it had already diagnosed the cause
(arm-fairness doctrine applied to shipped text), fixed it, and left both the reasoning and a
guard test behind. Copying a documented in-house fix beats re-deciding it.

**Not in scope, recommended separately:** an MCP server for entire-graph. It is the structural
reason the Graph instruction is unenforceable in Claude Code, but it is a build, not a fix.

---

## PR 1 — Retrieval returns usable output and reports what it dropped

Bottom of the stack. Nothing above matters if the tools error or lie.

**MCP response budget**
- `internal/cli/mcp.go`, `internal/cli/mcp_response_budget.go` — enforce a real byte/token ceiling
  on every `brain_*` response, not a notice. Truncate with an explicit, machine-readable marker
  naming what was dropped and how to get it (`--json`, a path, a narrower query).
- Worst offenders to verify: `brain_status`, `brain_brief`, `brain_impact`.

**Status latency (#325)**
- `internal/cli/verify_cmd.go:833` → `:424`, `internal/cli/agent_surface.go:1053` —
  `populateBrainStatusVerification` runs `git for-each-ref --contains <commit>` per distinct anchor
  commit, a full reachability walk. Gate verification behind `--details`; keep the summary cheap.

**The four HIGH silent-failure sites**
- `semantic.go:2380`/`:2518` — `FilterWarnings` substring match against `.brainignore`. Parse paths;
  never match on Detail text. Report a dropped-count.
- `regression.go:316`/`:1224` — `SkipAll` at 20000 scanned / 400 seen with no warning, then prints
  "No suspected regressions (scanned N files)". Emit a cap warning; correct the claim.
- `export.go:3588`,`:3619`/`:382` — `usefulExportWarnings` drops `checkpoint snapshot unavailable:`
  unless `--debug`, and the reported `warnings: %d` counts the filtered set.
- `distill_cmd.go:79` `capWarnings` — cap of 50 applied *before* persisting to the manifest, so the
  dropped text exists nowhere. Persist all; cap only the display.

**Truncated user-facing messages** (`status_render.go:264`, `statusCauseWidth=140`, byte-based)
- `semantic_stream.go:518` (182 chars), `semantic.go:1783` (173, still unfixed on main),
  `semantic.go:6720` (147). Shorten the strings; make truncation rune-aware.

## PR 2 — Multi-agent safety, indexing, and Windows

**#326 — `brain brief` takes `.git/index.lock`**
- `internal/cli/git_harden.go:78-81` is the single git spawn point and injects no
  `--no-optional-locks`. Add it there; swap `git diff --shortstat HEAD` → `diff-index`.
  Call sites: `semantic.go:2613`,`:2617`,`:5022`, `agent_surface.go:4768`.

**#327 — indexing stalls on a dirty worktree**
- `semantic.go:575` + `refresh.go:795-796`: dirty && !`--worktree` → `dirty_worktree` error, and
  needs-rebuild returns true unconditionally on dirty, so every refresh hits the refusal.
  `watch.go:305-309` aborts the whole tick, so the cursor never advances. Index HEAD via a temp
  tree; let watch skip only the semantic step. Same shape at `seed.go:276`.

**#328 — Ollama is loopback-only and never auto-selected**
- `refresh.go:829-840` `defaultRefreshAgent` tries codex→claude→none with ollama absent;
  `distill_cmd.go:2349` rejects a non-loopback `ENTIRE_BRAIN_OLLAMA_URL` **silently**;
  `watch.go:110` hardcodes `"codex"`; `embed.go:300` repeats the pattern.
  Add an opt-in remote host, add ollama to the auto order, and **warn loudly when a configured URL
  is ignored** — silent fallback to a cloud agent is the privacy bug in the report.

**#322 — Windows "command line is too long"**
- `distill.go:137`, exec at `distill_cmd.go:2237`: argv ends `"--system-prompt", <7516-byte
  prompt>`, blowing cmd.exe's 8191 limit. The chunk is already on stdin. Move the prompt to stdin
  or a temp file. ~15 callers share `distillAgentCommandArgs` (`seed.go:1830`, `facts_eval`,
  `facts_write_cmd`, `pattern_*`) — fix at the shared builder.
- **Verification limit, stated up front:** I cannot run Windows here. The test asserts the prompt
  is not on argv and that total argv stays under 8191, which is deterministic on any platform.

**#324 — `facts promote --keep-both` queues confidence-0 proposals**
- `internal/factmerge/admin.go:128` emits `Proposal{Action: ActionSupersede, Confidence: 0}` as a
  literal, with no similarity ever computed, once per same-path target — quadratic fanout.
  Compute similarity, or do not queue when confidence is 0. Callers: `factsync/sync.go:118`,
  `facts_sync_cmd.go`, `facts_admin_cmd.go`.

## PR 3 — The guide, the hook, and discovery

**Restore directive wording in brain's guide — port graph's fix**
- `internal/agentsetup/guide.go:8-9`,`:31`,`:68`,`:11-12` — align with entire-graph's text,
  including its `guide.go:8` header comment explaining why the two wordings must not be unified.
- `coordination_test.go:137` — remove `"FIRST action"`/`"SEARCH FIRST"` from the `bad` list and
  `"sufficient locations"` from the `want` list, keeping the genuine runtime-probe bans
  (`entire plugin list`, `command -v`, `setup.json`). Carry over graph's explanatory comment.
- Add brain's equivalent of `TestNormalGuideStaysDirective` so the regression cannot recur.
- `scripts/test-agent-coordination.py:69` — same ban, same change.

**#323 — the guide names a command that does not exist**
- `guide.go:33`,`:74`, `strict.go:66` hardcode `entire graph query`; entire-graph v0.4.0 dispatch
  has only `case "search"` (`query` lands in unreleased 0.5.0). Emit `search`, or probe
  `graph capabilities --json`. Same stale text at `docs/agent-coordination.md:107`.

**Wire the hook that already exists**
- `internal/cli/hook_cmd.go` (`hook pre-edit`, `hook post-failure`) is registered hidden at
  `root.go:169` and wired nowhere. Emit the `PreToolUse` wiring from `init-agents` so it lands in
  `.claude/settings.json` alongside the guide. Existing `PreToolUse` entries use
  `"matcher": "Agent"` only; this needs a Bash/Grep/Read matcher.

**MCP tool descriptions**
- `mcp.go:805-1030`, 37 tools. None say when to use the tool *instead of* grep. The description is
  what an agent reads when choosing; the guide is a file it may never open.

**In-repo docs**
- `README.md` — move the "What to ask" table (currently line 124 of 362) near the top and drop the
  Brain-command column, per Joseph's feedback. Fix its `query`→`recall` verbs for decision
  questions.
- `docs/agent-coordination.md:107` — stale `entire graph query`.

---

## Docs that are NOT in this repo

These live on the docs site, so they cannot be part of these PRs. They ship as a change list plus
an artifact (below), for whoever owns the site.

|---|---|

   appeared at repo level; doc ambiguity about where to run setup.
2. **Seven issues filed 2026-10-02** by two external testers (leine4550, peyton-alt).
3. **Two full agent transcripts** (Claude Code and Codex, same prompts, same repo) showing agents
   not using Brain or Graph.

Investigation of all three found that the headline problem is **not** that agents are habitual.

**Already fixed and merged:** #316 (semantic memo on the wrong path, unbounded, unlinearized),
#317 (ollama envelope cap measuring the prompt, silent truncation, probe on an exhausted budget,
usage-accounting bypass, misleading flag help). **Open and green:** #306, #318, #320, #321.

This plan covers what is *not* taken care of.

---

## The three root causes

### 1. Brain's guide instructs agents to skip the tools

`internal/agentsetup/files.go:1-3` claims the package is "mirrored byte-for-byte in both
repositories". It is not. entire-graph carries directive text; entire-brain still carries a
permissive regression from 2026-09-14.

| entire-graph `guide.go:78-81` | entire-brain `guide.go:8-9`, `:31`, `:68` |
|---|---|
| "Your FIRST action … **MUST** be ONE Graph query" | "**Directly inspect source** when the task already provides sufficient locations" |
| "Do not skip the query on the grounds that the available context feels sufficient" | "**Skip ceremonial queries** for small edits and follow-up work" |
| | "Useful locations from the brief do not require a redundant Graph query" |

Claude's own transcript: *"The agent guide says to start substantive tasks with `entire brain
brief` and use Graph for code discovery. I skipped that."* It was following the guide it was given.

**`internal/agentsetup/coordination_test.go:137` and `scripts/test-agent-coordination.py:69`
actively ban the strings `"FIRST action"` and `"SEARCH FIRST"`** — and the same test *requires*
`"sufficient locations"` to be present. The permissive wording is enforced by CI in both
directions. Verified directly, not taken from a report.

**Graph has already diagnosed and fixed this.** Its `coordination_test.go:142-145` says:

> *"'FIRST action' and 'SEARCH FIRST' used to be banned here alongside those probes. They are not
> probes; they are the directive that makes the product get used, and **banning them was benchmark
> arm-fairness doctrine applied to shipped text.**"*

That is the root cause, and it is a good mistake: arm-fairness is correct for benchmarks — you
cannot give one arm instructions the other lacks — and was then applied to the guide that ships to
users, where there is no other arm. Graph's `guide.go:8` now reads "TWO KINDS OF WORDING LIVE IN
THIS PACKAGE, AND THEY MUST NOT BE UNIFIED", and it added `TestNormalGuideStaysDirective`.

and documented**, for a cause graph already named. Brain never caught up.

exploration calls (0.34%), and the graph-first rate was 0 in every session sampled."*

From the Claude transcript, when finally instructed to run them:

| tool | result |
|---|---|
| `brain_status` | Error: 124,295 chars — exceeds maximum allowed tokens |
| `brain_brief` | Error: 125,822 chars — exceeds maximum allowed tokens |
| `brain_impact` | Error: 61,580 chars — exceeds maximum allowed tokens |
| `brain_entity_history` | `"matches": []` |
| `brain_regressions` | `"no code identifiers found"`, `scanned_files: 0` |

A context-saving tool that overflows context is worse than no tool. `mcp_response_budget.go:54`
exists but is only a byte-budget *notice*.

A sweep found four HIGH instances of the class that has already cost this project repeatedly.

*contains* a `.brainignore` pattern, by substring with no path parse. This repo's `.brainignore`
line 1 is `entire-brain`, a substring of every absolute path in it, so **every index warning is
discarded** and status reports a clean index that silently missed files.

  tree; let watch skip only the semantic step. Same shape at `seed.go:276`.

- `refresh.go:829-840` `defaultRefreshAgent` tries codex→claude→none with ollama absent;

**Guide text before enforcement hook.** The guide currently says the opposite of what we want;
changing text is free and addresses the cause. The hook is belt-and-braces and goes in the same
PR, but we measure the guide change on its own first so we learn which one worked.

**Port graph's fix rather than invent one.** I was ready to flag the directive-wording ban as
needing the author's sign-off. Checking graph first showed it had already diagnosed the cause
(arm-fairness doctrine applied to shipped text), fixed it, and left both the reasoning and a
guard test behind. Copying a documented in-house fix beats re-deciding it.

**Not in scope, recommended separately:** an MCP server for entire-graph. It is the structural
reason the Graph instruction is unenforceable in Claude Code, but it is a build, not a fix.

---

## PR 1 — Retrieval returns usable output and reports what it dropped

Bottom of the stack. Nothing above matters if the tools error or lie.

**MCP response budget**
- `internal/cli/mcp.go`, `internal/cli/mcp_response_budget.go` — enforce a real byte/token ceiling
  on every `brain_*` response, not a notice. Truncate with an explicit, machine-readable marker
  naming what was dropped and how to get it (`--json`, a path, a narrower query).
- Worst offenders to verify: `brain_status`, `brain_brief`, `brain_impact`.

**Status latency (#325)**
- `internal/cli/verify_cmd.go:833` → `:424`, `internal/cli/agent_surface.go:1053` —
  `populateBrainStatusVerification` runs `git for-each-ref --contains <commit>` per distinct anchor
  commit, a full reachability walk. Gate verification behind `--details`; keep the summary cheap.

**The four HIGH silent-failure sites**
- `semantic.go:2380`/`:2518` — `FilterWarnings` substring match against `.brainignore`. Parse paths;
  never match on Detail text. Report a dropped-count.
- `regression.go:316`/`:1224` — `SkipAll` at 20000 scanned / 400 seen with no warning, then prints
  "No suspected regressions (scanned N files)". Emit a cap warning; correct the claim.
- `export.go:3588`,`:3619`/`:382` — `usefulExportWarnings` drops `checkpoint snapshot unavailable:`
  unless `--debug`, and the reported `warnings: %d` counts the filtered set.
- `distill_cmd.go:79` `capWarnings` — cap of 50 applied *before* persisting to the manifest, so the
  dropped text exists nowhere. Persist all; cap only the display.

**Truncated user-facing messages** (`status_render.go:264`, `statusCauseWidth=140`, byte-based)
- `semantic_stream.go:518` (182 chars), `semantic.go:1783` (173, still unfixed on main),
  `semantic.go:6720` (147). Shorten the strings; make truncation rune-aware.

## PR 2 — Multi-agent safety, indexing, and Windows

**#326 — `brain brief` takes `.git/index.lock`**
- `internal/cli/git_harden.go:78-81` is the single git spawn point and injects no
  `--no-optional-locks`. Add it there; swap `git diff --shortstat HEAD` → `diff-index`.
  Call sites: `semantic.go:2613`,`:2617`,`:5022`, `agent_surface.go:4768`.

**#327 — indexing stalls on a dirty worktree**
- `semantic.go:575` + `refresh.go:795-796`: dirty && !`--worktree` → `dirty_worktree` error, and
  needs-rebuild returns true unconditionally on dirty, so every refresh hits the refusal.
  `watch.go:305-309` aborts the whole tick, so the cursor never advances. Index HEAD via a temp
  tree; let watch skip only the semantic step. Same shape at `seed.go:276`.

**#328 — Ollama is loopback-only and never auto-selected**
- `refresh.go:829-840` `defaultRefreshAgent` tries codex→claude→none with ollama absent;
  `distill_cmd.go:2349` rejects a non-loopback `ENTIRE_BRAIN_OLLAMA_URL` **silently**;
  `watch.go:110` hardcodes `"codex"`; `embed.go:300` repeats the pattern.
  Add an opt-in remote host, add ollama to the auto order, and **warn loudly when a configured URL
  is ignored** — silent fallback to a cloud agent is the privacy bug in the report.

**#322 — Windows "command line is too long"**
- `distill.go:137`, exec at `distill_cmd.go:2237`: argv ends `"--system-prompt", <7516-byte
  prompt>`, blowing cmd.exe's 8191 limit. The chunk is already on stdin. Move the prompt to stdin
  or a temp file. ~15 callers share `distillAgentCommandArgs` (`seed.go:1830`, `facts_eval`,
  `facts_write_cmd`, `pattern_*`) — fix at the shared builder.
- **Verification limit, stated up front:** I cannot run Windows here. The test asserts the prompt
  is not on argv and that total argv stays under 8191, which is deterministic on any platform.

**#324 — `facts promote --keep-both` queues confidence-0 proposals**
- `internal/factmerge/admin.go:128` emits `Proposal{Action: ActionSupersede, Confidence: 0}` as a
  literal, with no similarity ever computed, once per same-path target — quadratic fanout.
  Compute similarity, or do not queue when confidence is 0. Callers: `factsync/sync.go:118`,
  `facts_sync_cmd.go`, `facts_admin_cmd.go`.

## PR 3 — The guide, the hook, and discovery

**Restore directive wording in brain's guide — port graph's fix**
- `internal/agentsetup/guide.go:8-9`,`:31`,`:68`,`:11-12` — align with entire-graph's text,
  including its `guide.go:8` header comment explaining why the two wordings must not be unified.
- `coordination_test.go:137` — remove `"FIRST action"`/`"SEARCH FIRST"` from the `bad` list and
  `"sufficient locations"` from the `want` list, keeping the genuine runtime-probe bans
  (`entire plugin list`, `command -v`, `setup.json`). Carry over graph's explanatory comment.
- Add brain's equivalent of `TestNormalGuideStaysDirective` so the regression cannot recur.
- `scripts/test-agent-coordination.py:69` — same ban, same change.

**#323 — the guide names a command that does not exist**
- `guide.go:33`,`:74`, `strict.go:66` hardcode `entire graph query`; entire-graph v0.4.0 dispatch
  has only `case "search"` (`query` lands in unreleased 0.5.0). Emit `search`, or probe
  `graph capabilities --json`. Same stale text at `docs/agent-coordination.md:107`.

**Wire the hook that already exists**
- `internal/cli/hook_cmd.go` (`hook pre-edit`, `hook post-failure`) is registered hidden at
  `root.go:169` and wired nowhere. Emit the `PreToolUse` wiring from `init-agents` so it lands in
  `.claude/settings.json` alongside the guide. Existing `PreToolUse` entries use
  `"matcher": "Agent"` only; this needs a Bash/Grep/Read matcher.

**MCP tool descriptions**
- `mcp.go:805-1030`, 37 tools. None say when to use the tool *instead of* grep. The description is
  what an agent reads when choosing; the guide is a file it may never open.

**In-repo docs**
- `README.md` — move the "What to ask" table (currently line 124 of 362) near the top and drop the
  Brain-command column, per Joseph's feedback. Fix its `query`→`recall` verbs for decision
  questions.
- `docs/agent-coordination.md:107` — stale `entire graph query`.

---

## Docs that are NOT in this repo

These live on the docs site, so they cannot be part of these PRs. They ship as a change list plus
an artifact (below), for whoever owns the site.

| Page | Fix |
|---|---|
| Continuous Agent Memory | **"up to 71%" is a retracted figure** — that instance had the graph arm silently falling back to grep on a zero-byte payload and a 452-word stripped baseline. Replace with cost +2.49% (CI [−6.83, +11.18]) or drop the number. |
| Continuous Agent Memory | `entire/agent-guide.md` → `.entire/agent-guide.md` (leading dot) |
| Continuous Agent Memory | `entire graph stats --repo` errors without a value — drop the flag |
| Continuous Agent Memory | Remove the `entire graph stats` recommendation (reported 82.9M saved vs an honest ~46k) |
| Continuous Agent Memory | The rerun instruction is prose; make it a code block |
| Overview | **Add `entire brain init-agents` to the setup section** — `setup` never writes AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md, which is why Joseph saw nothing even from the repo root |
| Overview | "From your repository's root" → "…not from a cloned `entire-brain` directory" |
| Overview | `query` → `recall` for the decision example; document that facts are branch-scoped |
| Overview + Use Cases | Copy fixes: "For example,you can move"; "lessons that **has**"; the run-on "…and make sure to commit…" |
| Use Cases | `inspect impact --symbol X` **errors** (`unknown flag: --symbol`) — it is positional |
| All | Confirm the "CLI 0.10.0 or later" floor; no version gate exists in brain's source |

**Deliverable:** a two-tab artifact — tab 1 every problem with evidence and severity, tab 2 the
corrected pages as they should read.

---

## Verification

Each fix gets a reproduction that fails before and passes after. Mutation-verified: patch the
guard, prove the test goes red (`verified-by-weakening`).

| Fix | Reproduction |
|---|---|
| MCP budget | Call `brain_status`/`brain_brief`/`brain_impact` against a large repo; assert every response is under the cap and carries a dropped-marker |
| #325 | Brain with ~250 facts; assert `status --json` under a wall-clock threshold; assert `--details` still verifies |
| FilterWarnings | `.brainignore` containing a string that is a substring of an absolute path; assert warnings survive |
| regression cap | Corpus over 20000 files; assert a cap warning appears and the "no regressions" claim is qualified |
| export/capWarnings | Assert dropped warnings are persisted and recoverable |
| #326 | Hold a `brain brief` while running `git status` concurrently; assert no lock error. Deterministic form: assert `--no-optional-locks` in the spawn args |
| #327 | Dirty worktree + commit + refresh; assert the index advances rather than refusing |
| #328 | Non-loopback `ENTIRE_BRAIN_OLLAMA_URL`; assert a loud warning, and that opt-in remote works |
| #322 | Assert the prompt is not on argv and total argv < 8191 (platform-independent) |
| #324 | `promote --keep-both` over same-path facts; assert no confidence-0 proposals and no quadratic fanout |
| Guide | Assert the generated guide contains the directive sentence and names only commands the installed graph exposes |

**Loop:** run the full `internal/...` suite under `-race` (CI runs `-race`; local darwin does not),
re-run each reproduction, repeat until two consecutive passes find nothing new. One suite at a
time — concurrent runs contend over the global brain data dir and produce false failures.

### The usage experiment (the deeper ask)

`entire graph stats` already computes a **graph-first rate**, and graph's guide records the
baseline: 0.34% of calls, graph-first rate 0 in every session sampled.

1. Measure the baseline on a repo with the current permissive guide.
2. Install the corrected guide. Run a fleet of subagents on real tasks (locate, impact, "why did
   we"), each in its own worktree.
3. Re-measure graph-first rate.
4. Then enable the hook and measure again — so we learn whether wording alone was enough.
5. Collect each agent's own account of why it did or did not reach for the tool. That self-report
   is what exposed cause #1; it is the highest-yield signal we have.

---

## Sequencing

1. PR 1 — retrieval correctness (smallest, most obviously right, unblocks the stack)
2. PR 2 — multi-agent safety, indexing, Windows
3. PR 3 — guide, hook, discovery, in-repo docs
4. Docs artifact for the off-repo pages
5. Usage experiment, reported with before/after graph-first rate

Nothing merges without approval.

## Recommended, but not in these PRs

**An MCP server for entire-graph.** Brain ships 37 `brain_*` MCP tools; graph ships none. In
Claude Code the guide's "MUST run a Graph query" names a tool the agent does not have, so the
directive is unenforceable in the harness most users are in. This is the structural half of the
usage problem and the guide fix will only partly land without it. It is a build, not a fix, and
wants its own decision.

**Deferred with reasons, say the word to include:** nothing — all seven filed issues are in scope.
The only stated verification limit is #322, which cannot be executed on macOS; its test is
platform-independent but a real Windows run should confirm before closing the issue.

+	// window, and JSON of this shape runs about 2.5 characters per token --
+	// ids, quotes, braces and punctuation are not free -- so 128 KiB is roughly
+	// 52k tokens, double a typical client's whole tool-result ceiling.
+	// Measured from a real session: brain_status returned 124,295 characters,
+	// brain_brief 125,822 and brain_impact 61,580. Every one of them was UNDER
+	// the 128 KiB budget, so the trimming here worked exactly as designed, and
+	// every one was then REJECTED by the client as exceeding its token limit.

PR 1 is underway — MCP budget fixed and weakening-verified by me, three subagents on the rest.

## What I found that changed the plan

**My plan was wrong about the MCP budget, and the real cause is sharper.**

The budget isn't "only a notice" — it's a full implementation with bisection trimming, truncation markers and row-count repair. It worked perfectly. All three failing responses were **under** brain's 131,072-byte ceiling:

| tool | returned | under brain's budget? | client verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| `brain_status` | 124,295 | ✅ | **refused** |
| `brain_brief` | 125,822 | ✅ | **refused** |
| `brain_impact` | 61,580 | ✅ | **refused** |

The budget was calibrated to the **transport frame** (4 MiB), not to the **agent**. Its own comment says *"bound agent context below the transport frame limit"* — but 128 KiB of JSON is ~52k tokens at the ~2.5 chars/token this shape runs, double a client's whole tool-result ceiling. `brain_impact` is the tight bound: 61,580 chars ≈ 24.6k tokens, right at 25k.

Lowered to **32 KiB** (~13k tokens) with an `ENTIRE_BRAIN_MCP_MAX_BYTES` override, clamped to the frame limit.

**A test caught me, and it was half-right.** `TestTheResponseBudgetIsTheRetrievalBudgetNotAnArbitraryNumber` required the MCP budget to *equal* the retrieval budget. That coupling is the same mistake one level up — retrieval writes to a terminal where only bytes matter; MCP writes into a context window where tokens matter. I changed the invariant from equality to a ceiling (MCP must never emit *more* than retrieval) rather than deleting it, since the thing it was really protecting still holds.

Both weakenings go red with the real-world text:
> `budget 131072 is not below 61580, the smallest result a client actually refused`

## Still running

Three subagents on disjoint files: #325 status latency, the three silent warning-drops, and the `FilterWarnings` substring bug — that last one is the nastiest, since `.brainignore` line 1 in this very repo is `entire-brain`, a substring of every absolute path under it, so **every index warning is currently discarded** while status reports a clean index.

Each is required to verify by weakening and report the exact red assertion. I'll fold in their results, run the full suite under `-race` alone, then open PR 1 and move to PR 2.

content.text:
Verified. Two of three subagents are in; here's where PR 1 stands.

## Landed and weakening-verified

**MCP budget — the headline fix.** My plan had the cause wrong and I corrected it mid-flight. The trimming machinery was never broken; the budget was calibrated to the **4 MiB transport frame** instead of to the agent. All three failing responses were *under* brain's 131,072-byte ceiling and were then refused by the client. `brain_impact` sets the tight bound at 61,580 chars ≈ 24.6k tokens. Now **32 KiB** with an `ENTIRE_BRAIN_MCP_MAX_BYTES` override.

I also changed a test rather than deleting it: it required the MCP budget to *equal* the retrieval budget, which is the same mistake one level up — a terminal has no token limit, a context window does. The invariant is now a ceiling, which is what it was really protecting.

**#325 status latency — measured, not estimated.** Gated behind the existing `--details`. Live A/B on the real 961-fact brain: **24.19s → 2.42s**. Three weakening rounds, and the agent caught its own first draft passing vacuously because the fixture aborted before the expensive walk.

**`FilterWarnings` — the nastiest one.** It matched `.brainignore` patterns against free prose. In this very repo `.brainignore` line 1 is `entire-brain`, a substring of every absolute path under it, so **every index warning was being discarded** while status reported a clean index. Now parses paths, and reports a withheld count.

I verified its premise myself rather than take "indirect but strong": `Detail: serr.Error()` carries raw subprocess text, and `sanitizeSemanticWarningText` exists precisely to redact absolute paths out of it. That also confirms the filter must stay *before* sanitize — afterwards Detail is `<redacted>`.

**One thing I added on top.** Moving verification behind `--details` made the line silently disappear from `--verbose` — the exact defect class this PR is about. It now says `verification: not run (use --details; it walks git history)`, with a test proving it, and a second test proving it stays quiet at zero facts so it doesn't become noise.

## Outstanding

Agent 2 (the three silent warning-drops in `regression.go`, `export.go`, `distill_cmd.go`) is still running — it briefly broke the shared build twice mid-edit, which both other agents worked around.

Once it lands I'll run the full `internal/...` suite under `-race`, alone on the machine, then open PR 1. One risk I'm tracking: the new `warnings_hidden_by_brainignore` record is an added JSON field, and no agent could check golden-output tests broadly — the full suite is where that surfaces.

@RTK.md

## Entire repos: query the brain + graph BEFORE grepping

In any Entire repo (`cli`, `entire-api`, `entiredb`, `entire.io`, or a `devenv` worktree), prefer one brain/graph call over a grep+read sweep. For "where is / who calls / what depends on / what does this change break", ask FIRST; grep only as fallback.

- `entire sem edges|symbols --repo . --format ndjson` — callers/callees, definitions (file:line)
- `entire sem diff --base main --head HEAD` — what changed, entity-level
- entire-brain MCP tools: `brain_search`/`brain_code` (find by intent), `brain_impact` (blast radius), `brain_context`/`brain_brief` (task-scoped packet), `brain_query`/`brain_vsearch` (hybrid + vector), `brain_status` (which sources are live for this repo)

Run `brain_status` first — it reports whether facts/semantic are built for the repo you're in (the code graph is built for all; durable facts only where reported).

# RTK - Rust Token Killer

**Usage**: Token-optimized CLI proxy (60-90% savings on dev operations)

## Meta Commands (always use rtk directly)

```bash
rtk gain              # Show token savings analytics
rtk gain --history    # Show command usage history with savings
rtk discover          # Analyze Claude Code history for missed opportunities
rtk proxy <cmd>       # Execute raw command without filtering (for debugging)
```

## Installation Verification

```bash
rtk --version         # Should show: rtk X.Y.Z
rtk gain              # Should work (not "command not found")
which rtk             # Verify correct binary
```

⚠️ **Name collision**: If `rtk gain` fails, you may have reachingforthejack/rtk (Rust Type Kit) installed instead.

## Hook-Based Usage

All other commands are automatically rewritten by the Claude Code hook.
Example: `git status` → `rtk git status` (transparent, 0 tokens overhead)

Refer to CLAUDE.md for full command reference.

# devenv — Entire org local dev

@CODEBASE-MAP.md

- Full-suite architecture map above. Keep it updated in place; do not re-discover.
- Main checkouts (`cli/`, `entiredb/`, `entire.io/`, `entire-api/`) may hold uncommitted work — never commit there. One fresh worktree/clone per task (`cli-<NNNN>/` etc).
- Local stack: `mise run dev` (see map §3). Users: `admin/admin1234`, `test/password1234`. UI: http://localhost:5173/login.
- Per-repo build/test commands: map §9. cli pre-commit gate: `mise run check`. Real-agent e2e (`mise run test:e2e`) costs money — never run proactively.

---

## Launch sessions inside the repo, never from devenv/

Claude Code loads project settings from the directory the session was **launched** in. Each
product repo (`entire-brain/`, `entire-graph/`, `cli/`, ...) carries Entire's capture hooks in its
own `.claude/settings.json` plus `.entire/settings.json` with `enabled: true`. **`devenv/` carries
neither**, so a session rooted here records nothing — no sessions, no checkpoints — and says
nothing about it. Any PR opened from such a session gets a trail with **no session attached**.

    cd ~/devenv/entire-brain && claude      # captured
    cd ~/devenv && claude                   # NOT captured

This is silent by default and has already cost a four-day run: 15 commits across three branches
with zero captured sessions, noticed only when someone asked why the trails were empty. A
`SessionStart` guard now announces it (`.claude/hooks/warn-capture-off.sh`), but the guard only
tells you — it cannot capture retroactively.

**Do not "fix" this by running `entire enable` in `devenv/`.** devenv is its own repo
(`entirehq/devenv`) with its own remote, so checkpoints for work done inside a sub-repo would
attach to the devenv repo and the wrong trail. Mis-attributed sessions are worse than none.
Orchestrating across repos from `devenv/` is fine when you do not need capture — just know that
you do not have it.

## You are the ORCHESTRATOR — delegate, don't grind

Default mode: **you plan, route and verify; sub-agents do the work.** Spawn them with the Agent
tool (or `Workflow` for parallel fan-out). Do not personally execute long mechanical work you
could hand off.

| tier | when | how |
|---|---|---|
| **Opus 5** | judgement, design, adversarial verification, anything where being wrong is expensive | `Agent(model: "opus")` |
| **Sonnet 5** | bounded mechanical work: extraction, scripted analysis, file sweeps, log triage | `Agent(model: "sonnet")` |

Rules that override convenience:
- **Every sub-agent prompt must ask for caveman-ultra compressed output and RTK use.** Their tool
  output does not reach you; only their report does, so make it dense.
- **Adversarially verify before believing.** Any finding that will change a decision gets N
  skeptics told to default to *refuted* unless they independently reproduce it. This has killed
  ~45% of claims in practice, including the orchestrator's own.
- **Live verification over assertion.** Run the thing. A claim without a command behind it is a
  hypothesis.
- **No AI attribution footers in commits.**
- **Reproduce-proven-results doctrine:** treat every task as already achieved by someone; "no" or
  "impossible" is never a terminal answer — go one layer deeper (transcripts, harness, source).

## Two-agent split (current)

Two Claude Code agents run in parallel on this machine and must not collide.

| agent | owns | notes file |
|---|---|---|
| **graph-bench** | entire-graph token benchmarks, graphmark harness, rep30/rep100/300 cells | `graph-bench-results/TokensNotes.md` |
| **memory-bench** | memory/recall benchmarks (LOCOMO, prose-memory, cmm parity) | `graph-bench-results/MemoryNotes.md` |

**Coordinate through `AGENT-COMMS.md`** (repo root). Read it at the start of a session and before
touching anything the other agent owns. Protocol and message format are defined in that file.

Shared, do not stomp:
- `graphmark/` (entirehq/graphmark; formerly `graphmark-bench/`, which no longer exists) — the benchmark harness. Announce in comms before editing its runner/scorer.
- GCP VMs `graphbench-a..d` — claim a VM in comms before launching cells on it.
- **Never `scp` a script onto a VM while sessions are running.** Bash reads scripts lazily;
  overwriting in place moves bytes under a running shell and corrupts live runs (this destroyed 22
  sessions). Deploy to a temp path and atomic `mv`.

## Benchmark doctrine (read before quoting any number)

Full ledger of what is live and what is struck: **`graph-bench-results/TokensNotes.md`**.
Method drill: the `graph-bench-forensics` skill.

Non-negotiables:
- **Fairness:** tool *output* differences are legitimate; arm-asymmetric *instructions* are not.
  Test — *would this sentence help an arm with no tool?* If yes, both arms or neither.
- **Gate:** a pair counts only if both arms `subtype=="success"` AND non-empty patch. Drop
  symmetrically.
- **Power:** MDE is ~25–26 points at n=30. Never read sub-groups of 3–7 inside one cell. Always
  report a bootstrap CI and the median beside the total.
- **Never replicate an instance; always add instances.** Run-level noise is ~87% of paired variance.
- **Audit the harness before blaming the tool.** Every withdrawn headline here died of a harness
  bug. See TokensNotes §5 for the ten silent-failure modes already found.

## Code intelligence: query the brain + graph BEFORE grepping

Every main checkout has an Entire brain. Its **code graph** is built for all repos; **durable
facts** where the brain reports them. One graph/brain call beats a grep+read sweep. For "where is /
who calls / what depends on / what does this change break", ask FIRST; grep only as fallback.

# Entire — Codebase Map

> Full-suite architecture map for the `devenv/` monorepo-of-repos. Regenerated 2026-07-16
> from live exploration of the four core repos. Keep this updated in place; do not re-discover.

## 1. What Entire is

Entire wraps AI coding agents (Claude Code, Gemini, OpenCode, Cursor, Factory Droid,
Copilot, Pi) with automatic **session + checkpoint capture**. Agent work is committed as
signed checkpoints to a git-native distributed store, attributed to authors, and surfaced
through a web app as **trails** (PR-like work threads) with viewer, code review, search,
recaps, and repo dashboards. GitHub-OAuth gated; residency/jurisdiction-aware.

## 2. Repos in `devenv/` (canonical checkouts)

| Dir | Lang/stack | Role |
|---|---|---|
| `cli/` | Go 1.26, cobra + charm/huh | The `entire` CLI + `git-remote-entire` helper. Captures agent sessions, writes checkpoints, talks to Core + cells. |
| `entiredb/` | Go, go-git v6, DHT | Distributed git-native storage. Splits into **entire-server** (data plane) + **entire-core** (control plane). |
| `entire-api/` | Go, chi + Huma v2, Postgres, NATS | Per-jurisdiction ("cell") activity read API + 2 NATS workers. Successor to `entire.io/api` activity endpoints. |
| `entire.io/` | React 19 / Vite 7 + Cloudflare Workers (Hono) | The web app: frontend + BFF `api/` + marketing `website/`. |
| `git-meta-service-gm-heads/` | Go, K8s | git-meta exchange format service; writes reserved `refs/meta/entire/*`, Postgres read-model, NATS sync. An entire-api workload (ENT-1106). |

Everything else (`cli-1439/`, `entire-api-261/`, `entiredb-gm-heads/`, …) = **git worktrees /
branch clones** off the four core repos, per the isolation doctrine. Not separate products.

## 4. Data / control plane split (entiredb)

- **Data plane (`entire-server`)** — git smart-HTTP, refs, objects, replication.
  - Storage engine at repo root: `objstore/` (DISS store; `Cid = RepoID+type+hash`, BadgerDB
    local + DHT replication), `refstore/` (Postgres `refs` table, `(repo_id,ref_name)` CAS),
    `packfile/`, `gitutil/`, `diss/`.
  - `dht/` — Kademlia keyed by RepoID (repo-locality). memberlist gossip `:9999`, provider
    records, `repair_queue.go`/`repair_claims.go` (atomic repair of under-replicated repos),
    quorum writes to K-closest, `FindProviders` reads. **No Raft** — correctness from
    content-addressing + Postgres ref CAS + quorum replication.
- **Control plane (`entire-core`)** — identity, OAuth/OIDC, JWKS, SpiceDB authz, repo
  lifecycle. CockroachDB + SpiceDB. `core/identity|authn|authz`, `core/registry|resource|
  repoadmin|provisionerr`, `core/coreapi` (Huma `/api/v1` + login/token), `core/regional|
  audit|oidcfed|erasure*` (GDPR/PII/juris), `core/githubapp|githubtokens|mirror*`,
  `core/repofacts` (mTLS Connect — cells push git facts, consumed by entire-api).
- **cmd/**: `entire-server`, `entire-core`, `entire-repo` (data-plane git CLI), `entiredbctl`
  (operator), `entire-backup` (git-bundle S3/fs), `entire-deploy`, `entire-ci(+webhooks)`,
  `entire-mock-idp`, `authz-probe`.

## 5. entire-api (per-jurisdiction cells)

- **One module → 3 processes over 2 Postgres schemas.** Git content is *never* replicated —
  read through to entiredb at request time, cached by branch tip. Local stores hold only
  product overlay + metadata (pointers + aggregates, never content).
- `cmd/api` — HTTP server, `/api/v1/*` (`/me`, `/repos`, `/projects`) + entiredb git plane
  sub-pathed `/api/v1/git/*`; single OpenAPI at `/api/v1/openapi.yaml`.
- `cmd/repo-activity` — worker: ref ingester (Stage1 `pull repo_refs_v1` → classify → enqueue;
  Stage2 drain `repo_index_jobs`) + forwarder publisher + checkpoint-analysis (Anthropic).
- `cmd/user-activity` — worker: forwarder consumer → user store.
- Stores (separate pool + Postgres role, no cross-schema joins):
  - **repo store** — `repos`, `checkpoints`, `sessions`, `checkpoint_commits`, `repo_branch_tip`,
    `repo_author_day`, `repo_checkpoint_analyses`, `github_repo_meta`, trails/review tables.
  - **user store** — `my_activity` (residency-safe, monthly-partitioned by `committed_at`,
    ULID `origin_key`, metadata-only), `user_preferences`, `user_repo_preferences`.
- Migrations: **goose, embedded, UTC-timestamp filenames** `YYYYMMDDHHMMSS_<name>.sql` via
  `scripts/new-migration.sh <repo|user> <name>` — never hand-picked integers (silent-skip
  hazard). Never edit merged migrations.
- Integrations: NATS (per-region island; streams `repo_refs_v1`, `repo_index_jobs`
  (+`_backfill`), `repo_checkpoint_analysis_jobs`, `user_activity_v1`,
  `resource_lifecycle_v1`, `github_meta_v1`, `github_pr_v1`, `repo_settings_v1`,
  `trail_events_v1`; cross-region = direct publish, no supercluster),
  regional read-only SpiceDB, entiredb Repo API (mTLS git read-through), entire-core mTLS
  (JWKS, STS token exchange), Anthropic (analysis labels via Cloudflare AI Gateway, gated by
  `ANALYZE_CHECKPOINTS`/`ANALYZE_CHECKPOINTS_LLM`, usage-cap park+replay). Federation is
  client-driven.
- **Trails subsystem** (RFD-023 native port): gates/gate-settings, approvals, mergeability,
  threads/messages, reviews/comments, attachments (S3 presigned via `internal/trailblobs`),
  runner ingest/monitors. Dual-addressed: legacy `/trails/{host}/{owner}/{repo}/...` and
  platform `/repos/{repo_id}/trails/...`. Session shares = encrypted S3 snapshots with
  wrapped DEK (crypto-shred on unshare).

- entiredb: **no Raft** (`20260320-no-raft`), reserved refs `refs/meta/entire/*`
  (`20260603-reserved-refs`), entire-api split (`20260622`).
- Two distinct "api": Go **`entire-api`** (cells) vs TS **`entire.io/api`** (BFF). Don't conflate.
- Content is never copied into product stores — always read-through to entiredb by branch tip.
- `start-dev.sh` carries stale Rails + Raft labels (see §3).
- Root `README.md`/`Onboarding.md` say setup clones "entire" — `setup-repos.sh` actually
  clones `entiredb` + `entire.io` + `cli`. Docs drifted.

## 11. git-meta-service (detail)

- Implements the [git-meta](https://git-meta.com) exchange format as an API: `(target,key,value)`
  metadata (string/list/set) on commits/branches/paths/change-ids/project, byte-compatible with
  the upstream Rust `git meta` CLI (golden test round-trips vs real CLI if installed).
- **Write path**: serialize → CAS-push to `refs/meta/main` in entiredb (go-git v6 smart HTTP,
  forwards caller's JWT so push authz matches) → materialize into Postgres read-model. Git is
  source of truth; Postgres rebuildable. NATS consumer materializes out-of-band CLI pushes
  (read-only mTLS identity).
- **API** `/api/v1/repos/{repoId}/meta/*`: set/rm, list push/rm, set add/rm, cas (412 precondition /
  409 ref-race), GET query (`target`/`key`/`prefix`). Huma v2 OpenAPI; scoped-JWT bearer auth.
- **STATUS 2026-08-29 — the standalone service is an ARCHIVED POC.** `entirehq/git-meta-service`
  is read-only ("The real thing is now part of entire-api"). **The supported implementation is
  `entire-api/internal/gitmeta` + `internal/metaengine` + `internal/httpapi/repos_gitmeta.go`** —
  substantial, not a stub. Build clients against that, never the POC.
- **Both former entiredb blockers are RESOLVED** (this section was stale): (a) ADR
  `20260603-reserved-refs` was amended 2026-07-23 to narrow the reservation from all of
  `refs/meta/*` to just `refs/meta/entire/*`, enforcement moved to `refpolicy/refpolicy.go`
  (called at `server/githttp/receive_pack.go:459`); (b) no separate `git-meta` workload is needed —
  `WorkloadEntireAPI` is admitted for entire-api's git-meta receive-pack writes to
  `refs/meta/entire/*` (`svctok_listener.go:419`, ENT-1106). **git-meta can ship, and in
  entire-api it already has.**
- Auth (POC) verified fail-closed **at the binary level** (`go tool nm` links only
  `NotConfiguredAuthenticator`; dev authenticators are all `//go:build gitmeta_dev`, no manifest
  sets the tag). Token repoID is checked against request repoID (403) and pull/push scope is
  enforced per operation (403). entire-api's implementation has **no dev-token path at all**.
- **Two caveats for anything building on it** (e.g. brain fact heads): CAS conflict classification
  rests on **substring-matching go-git/entiredb error text** — flagged fragile in-code, pinned to
  the go.mod version, and it will break silently on a go-git upgrade (typed errors = the durable
  fix). And **CAS-create is NOT a mutual-exclusion primitive**: two writers converging on a
  byte-identical commit BOTH get success, so leader-election use must write a writer-unique value.
- Byte-compatibility with the upstream Rust CLI was **never executed in CI** (golden test `t.Skip`s
  when the CLI is absent, and nothing installed it) — now wired by entire-api **PR #932**, which
  ran green in CI: `git meta 0.1.12`, round-trip tree OID `8a942fee…`. The claim is TRUE, it was
  merely unverified. Trap: `cargo install git-meta` installs the WRONG crate; use **`git-meta-cli`**.
- Local dev: docker-compose Postgres :55432, NATS :54222/:58222. Checkout
  `git-meta-service-gm-heads/` on branch `gm-heads-service` with dirty tree (engine/api/store/
  gitclient edits + untracked `cmd/gitmeta-localtrial`, `cmd/gitmeta-verify`, `cas_test.go`)
  as of 2026-07-16.

# entire-graph — instructions for coding agents (follow directly)

You have a deterministic local code graph: `entire graph` (functions, classes, methods,
types, routes + call/inheritance relations; no network). These instructions are FOR YOU, the
agent reading this file. Use the graph to narrow exploration without trading away correctness.

## The workflow (mandatory for locate/fix/change tasks)

Your FIRST action on any task that requires finding code must be ONE search:

    entire graph search --repo . --profile full --query "<the task or bug in one sentence>"

Then open the top hit's file with your file-read tool (pass a line range around the reported
line), inspect enough surrounding behavior to justify the change, and make the smallest complete
edit. Treat graph output as evidence, not an oracle.

## Hard rules

1. SEARCH FIRST — never grep/find/cat to locate code before you have searched.
2. READ focused source around the result. Widen the check when aliases, generated code, dynamic
   dispatch, or related implementations could matter.
3. Use graph follow-ups only when they answer a real question. For impact or callers, prefer:
       entire graph impact --repo . --symbol X
4. Make the smallest complete edit and check sibling sites or contracts when the task implies them.
5. VERIFY before stopping. Run the most focused relevant test, build, or reproduction available.
   If execution is unavailable, perform a bounded source-level verification and state the limit.
6. Prefer precise queries and line ranges, but never trade resolution for fewer turns.
7. Feature-detect before relying on semantic relations:
       entire graph capabilities --json

## When NOT to use the graph

If the task already names the exact file and it is small, just read it — the graph saves tokens
by eliminating exploration; when there is nothing to explore, skip it.

## Reference

    locate  ->  entire graph search --repo . --profile full --query "..."
    impact  ->  entire graph impact --repo . --symbol X   (one shot: callers, callees, type consumers, data flow, co-change, siblings)
    callers ->  entire graph neighbors --repo . --symbol X --relation CALLS --direction in
    change  ->  entire graph diff --base A --head B --json
    detect  ->  entire graph capabilities --json   (inventory-only languages have no relations)
    stats   ->  entire graph stats --repo .        (human-facing token-savings report; not part of your workflow — do not run it unless asked)

@CODEBASE-MAP.md

- Full-suite architecture map above. Keep it updated in place; do not re-discover.
- Main checkouts (`cli/`, `entiredb/`, `entire.io/`, `entire-api/`) may hold uncommitted work — never commit there. One fresh worktree/clone per task (`cli-<NNNN>/` etc).

---

## Launch sessions inside the repo, never from devenv/

Claude Code loads project settings from the directory the session was **launched** in. Each
product repo (`entire-brain/`, `entire-graph/`, `cli/`, ...) carries Entire's capture hooks in its
own `.claude/settings.json` plus `.entire/settings.json` with `enabled: true`. **`devenv/` carries
neither**, so a session rooted here records nothing — no sessions, no checkpoints — and says
nothing about it. Any PR opened from such a session gets a trail with **no session attached**.

    cd ~/devenv/entire-brain && claude      # captured
    cd ~/devenv && claude                   # NOT captured

This is silent by default and has already cost a four-day run: 15 commits across three branches
with zero captured sessions, noticed only when someone asked why the trails were empty. A
`SessionStart` guard now announces it (`.claude/hooks/warn-capture-off.sh`), but the guard only
tells you — it cannot capture retroactively.

**Do not "fix" this by running `entire enable` in `devenv/`.** devenv is its own repo
(`entirehq/devenv`) with its own remote, so checkpoints for work done inside a sub-repo would
attach to the devenv repo and the wrong trail. Mis-attributed sessions are worse than none.
Orchestrating across repos from `devenv/` is fine when you do not need capture — just know that
you do not have it.

## You are the ORCHESTRATOR — delegate, don't grind

Default mode: **you plan, route and verify; sub-agents do the work.** Spawn them with the Agent
tool (or `Workflow` for parallel fan-out). Do not personally execute long mechanical work you
could hand off.

| tier | when | how |
|---|---|---|
| **Opus 5** | judgement, design, adversarial verification, anything where being wrong is expensive | `Agent(model: "opus")` |
| **Sonnet 5** | bounded mechanical work: extraction, scripted analysis, file sweeps, log triage | `Agent(model: "sonnet")` |

Rules that override convenience:
- **Every sub-agent prompt must ask for caveman-ultra compressed output and RTK use.** Their tool
  output does not reach you; only their report does, so make it dense.
- **Adversarially verify before believing.** Any finding that will change a decision gets N
  skeptics told to default to *refuted* unless they independently reproduce it. This has killed
  ~45% of claims in practice, including the orchestrator's own.
- **Live verification over assertion.** Run the thing. A claim without a command behind it is a
  hypothesis.
- **No AI attribution footers in commits.**
- **Reproduce-proven-results doctrine:** treat every task as already achieved by someone; "no" or
  "impossible" is never a terminal answer — go one layer deeper (transcripts, harness, source).

## Two-agent split (current)

Two Claude Code agents run in parallel on this machine and must not collide.

| agent | owns | notes file |
|---|---|---|

> Full-suite architecture map for the `devenv/` monorepo-of-repos. Regenerated 2026-07-16
> from live exploration of the four core repos. Keep this updated in place; do not re-discover.

## 1. What Entire is

Entire wraps AI coding agents (Claude Code, Gemini, OpenCode, Cursor, Factory Droid,
Copilot, Pi) with automatic **session + checkpoint capture**. Agent work is committed as
signed checkpoints to a git-native distributed store, attributed to authors, and surfaced
through a web app as **trails** (PR-like work threads) with viewer, code review, search,
recaps, and repo dashboards. GitHub-OAuth gated; residency/jurisdiction-aware.

## 2. Repos in `devenv/` (canonical checkouts)

| Dir | Lang/stack | Role |

| `entiredb/` | Go, go-git v6, DHT | Distributed git-native storage. Splits into **entire-server** (data plane) + **entire-core** (control plane). |
| `entire-api/` | Go, chi + Huma v2, Postgres, NATS | Per-jurisdiction ("cell") activity read API + 2 NATS workers. Successor to `entire.io/api` activity endpoints. |
| `entire.io/` | React 19 / Vite 7 + Cloudflare Workers (Hono) | The web app: frontend + BFF `api/` + marketing `website/`. |
| `git-meta-service-gm-heads/` | Go, K8s | git-meta exchange format service; writes reserved `refs/meta/entire/*`, Postgres read-model, NATS sync. An entire-api workload (ENT-1106). |

Everything else (`cli-1439/`, `entire-api-261/`, `entiredb-gm-heads/`, …) = **git worktrees /
branch clones** off the four core repos, per the isolation doctrine. Not separate products.

# entire-graph — instructions for coding agents (follow directly)

You have a deterministic local code graph: `entire graph` (functions, classes, methods,
types, routes + call/inheritance relations; no network). These instructions are FOR YOU, the
agent reading this file. Use the graph to narrow exploration without trading away correctness.

## The workflow (mandatory for locate/fix/change tasks)

Your FIRST action on any task that requires finding code must be ONE search:

    entire graph search --repo . --profile full --query "<the task or bug in one sentence>"

Then open the top hit's file with your file-read tool (pass a line range around the reported
line), inspect enough surrounding behavior to justify the change, and make the smallest complete
edit. Treat graph output as evidence, not an oracle.

## Hard rules

1. SEARCH FIRST — never grep/find/cat to locate code before you have searched.
2. READ focused source around the result. Widen the check when aliases, generated code, dynamic
   dispatch, or related implementations could matter.
3. Use graph follow-ups only when they answer a real question. For impact or callers, prefer:
       entire graph impact --repo . --symbol X
4. Make the smallest complete edit and check sibling sites or contracts when the task implies them.
5. VERIFY before stopping. Run the most focused relevant test, build, or reproduction available.
   If execution is unavailable, perform a bounded source-level verification and state the limit.
6. Prefer precise queries and line ranges, but never trade resolution for fewer turns.
7. Feature-detect before relying on semantic relations:
       entire graph capabilities --json

## When NOT to use the graph

If the task already names the exact file and it is small, just read it — the graph saves tokens
by eliminating exploration; when there is nothing to explore, skip it.

## Reference

# entire-graph — instructions for coding agents (follow directly)

You have a deterministic local code graph: `entire graph` (functions, classes, methods,
types, routes + call/inheritance relations; no network). These instructions are FOR YOU, the
agent reading this file. Use the graph to narrow exploration without trading away correctness.

## The workflow (mandatory for locate/fix/change tasks)

Your FIRST action on any task that requires finding code must be ONE search:

    entire graph search --repo . --profile full --query "<the task or bug in one sentence>"

Then open the top hit's file with your file-read tool (pass a line range around the reported
line), inspect enough surrounding behavior to justify the change, and make the smallest complete
edit. Treat graph output as evidence, not an oracle.

## Hard rules

1. SEARCH FIRST — never grep/find/cat to locate code before you have searched.
2. READ focused source around the result. Widen the check when aliases, generated code, dynamic
   dispatch, or related implementations could matter.
3. Use graph follow-ups only when they answer a real question. For impact or callers, prefer:
       entire graph impact --repo . --symbol X
4. Make the smallest complete edit and check sibling sites or contracts when the task implies them.
5. VERIFY before stopping. Run the most focused relevant test, build, or reproduction available.

6. Prefer precise queries and line ranges, but never trade resolution for fewer turns.
7. Feature-detect before relying on semantic relations:
       entire graph capabilities --json

If the task already names the exact file and it is small, just read it — the graph saves tokens
by eliminating exploration; when there is nothing to explore, skip it.

|---|---|

| `brain_brief` | Error: 125,822 chars — exceeds maximum allowed tokens |

| Continuous Agent Memory | `entire graph stats --repo` errors without a value — drop the flag |

| Overview | "From your repository's root" → "…not from a cloned `entire-brain` directory" |

| Overview + Use Cases | Copy fixes: "For example,you can move"; "lessons that **has**"; the run-on "…and make sure to commit…" |
| Use Cases | `inspect impact --symbol X` **errors** (`unknown flag: --symbol`) — it is positional |
| All | Confirm the "CLI 0.10.0 or later" floor; no version gate exists in brain's source |

corrected pages as they should read.

---

Each fix gets a reproduction that fails before and passes after. Mutation-verified: patch the
guard, prove the test goes red (`verified-by-weakening`).

| Fix | Reproduction |
|---|---|
| MCP budget | Call `brain_status`/`brain_brief`/`brain_impact` against a large repo; assert every response is under the cap and carries a dropped-marker |
| #325 | Brain with ~250 facts; assert `status --json` under a wall-clock threshold; assert `--details` still verifies |
| FilterWarnings | `.brainignore` containing a string that is a substring of an absolute path; assert warnings survive |
| regression cap | Corpus over 20000 files; assert a cap warning appears and the "no regressions" claim is qualified |
| export/capWarnings | Assert dropped warnings are persisted and recoverable |
| #326 | Hold a `brain brief` while running `git status` concurrently; assert no lock error. Deterministic form: assert `--no-optional-locks` in the spawn args |
| #327 | Dirty worktree + commit + refresh; assert the index advances rather than refusing |
| #328 | Non-loopback `ENTIRE_BRAIN_OLLAMA_URL`; assert a loud warning, and that opt-in remote works |
| #322 | Assert the prompt is not on argv and total argv < 8191 (platform-independent) |
| #324 | `promote --keep-both` over same-path facts; assert no confidence-0 proposals and no quadratic fanout |
| Guide | Assert the generated guide contains the directive sentence and names only commands the installed graph exposes |

**Loop:** run the full `internal/...` suite under `-race` (CI runs `-race`; local darwin does not),
re-run each reproduction, repeat until two consecutive passes find nothing new. One suite at a
time — concurrent runs contend over the global brain data dir and produce false failures.

### The usage experiment (the deeper ask)

`entire graph stats` already computes a **graph-first rate**, and graph's guide records the
baseline: 0.34% of calls, graph-first rate 0 in every session sampled.

1. Measure the baseline on a repo with the current permissive guide.
2. Install the corrected guide. Run a fleet of subagents on real tasks (locate, impact, "why did
   we"), each in its own worktree.
3. Re-measure graph-first rate.
4. Then enable the hook and measure again — so we learn whether wording alone was enough.
5. Collect each agent's own account of why it did or did not reach for the tool. That self-report
   is what exposed cause #1; it is the highest-yield signal we have.

---

## Sequencing

1. PR 1 — retrieval correctness (smallest, most obviously right, unblocks the stack)
2. PR 2 — multi-agent safety, indexing, Windows
3. PR 3 — guide, hook, discovery, in-repo docs
4. Docs artifact for the off-repo pages
5. Usage experiment, reported with before/after graph-first rate

Nothing merges without approval.

## Recommended, but not in these PRs

**An MCP server for entire-graph.** Brain ships 37 `brain_*` MCP tools; graph ships none. In
Claude Code the guide's "MUST run a Graph query" names a tool the agent does not have, so the
directive is unenforceable in the harness most users are in. This is the structural half of the
usage problem and the guide fix will only partly land without it. It is a build, not a fix, and
wants its own decision.

**Deferred with reasons, say the word to include:** nothing — all seven filed issues are in scope.
The only stated verification limit is #322, which cannot be executed on macOS; its test is
platform-independent but a real Windows run should confirm before closing the issue.
